A content source that can be an inline string, read from a file, or fetched from a URL. Used for release header/footer values.

YAML examples:

```yaml
header: "inline text"
header:
  from_file: ./RELEASE_HEADER.md
header:
  from_url: https://example.com/header.md
header:
  from_url: https://example.com/header.md
  headers:
    X-API-Token: "{{ Env.API_TOKEN }}"
    Accept: "text/markdown"
```

Both `from_file` path and `from_url` URL are template-rendered before use. Header values are template-rendered.

headers.description: Optional HTTP headers (value templates allowed). Enables private mirrors and authenticated endpoints.

after.description: Hooks that run inside THIS crate's scope at the end of the release, after the crate's publish dispatch (and post-publish verification) completes. Per-crate counterpart of the top-level `after:` (which fires once around the whole release). Same per-crate firing semantics across all modes, template variables, and abort semantics as the per-crate `before:`.

app_bundles.description: macOS app bundle configurations for this crate.

archives.description: Archive configurations for this crate. Set to false to disable archiving, or provide an array of archive configs.

before.description:
Hooks that run inside THIS crate's scope at the start of the release, before the build. Distinct from the top-level `before:`, which fires ONCE around the whole release; these fire once per crate with that crate's version/tag template vars anchored, so `cmd` / `dir` / `env` / `if` render against the crate's own `Version` / `Tag` / `ProjectName`. A non-zero exit aborts the release.

Fires once per crate in EVERY multi-crate mode — workspace per-crate AND workspace lockstep with multiple publisher crates — in both a full `anodizer release` and `anodizer release --publish-only`, matching the per-crate iteration of `before_publish:` and the publishers. With an explicit `--crate` subset only the selected crates' hooks fire. No-op in a single-crate config with no `crates:` block (use the top-level `before:` there).

before_publish.description: Hooks that run immediately before THIS crate's publishers dispatch, once per matching artifact (the same per-artifact semantics as the top-level `before_publish:`), scoped to the crate's own artifacts and template vars. Honors the per-entry `ids:` / `artifacts:` filters. A non-zero exit aborts the release before that crate publishes to any registry. The top-level `before_publish:` still fires once over the full artifact set; this one targets a single crate's artifacts.

binstall.description: cargo-binstall metadata configuration for this crate.

blobs.description: Cloud storage (S3/GCS/Azure) upload configurations for this crate.

builds.description: Build configurations for this crate. One entry per binary by default.

cross.description: Cross-compilation strategy for this crate: auto, zigbuild, cross, or cargo.

depends_on.description: Other crates this crate depends on; ensures release ordering.

dmgs.description: macOS DMG disk image configurations for this crate.

docker_digest.description: Docker image digest file configuration for this crate.

docker_manifests.description: Docker multi-platform manifest configurations for this crate.

dockers_v2.description: Docker V2 image build configurations for this crate (canonical API: images+tags, annotations, build_args, sbom, disable). The legacy `docker:` block was removed; this is the only docker block. The `docker_v2:` spelling is still accepted via serde alias for back-compat.

flatpaks.description: Linux Flatpak bundle configurations for this crate.

msis.description: Windows MSI installer configurations for this crate.

name.description: Crate name as published (must match the Cargo.toml package name).

nfpms.description: Linux package (deb, rpm, apk) configurations for this crate. Renamed from `nfpm:` (singular) for spelling parity with `Defaults.nfpms` and the rest of the plural-name per-crate packaging lists (`dmgs`, `msis`, `pkgs`, `nsis`, ...). The `nfpm:` spelling is still accepted via serde alias for back-compat.

no_unique_dist_dir.description: When true (or template evaluating to "true"), all build outputs are placed in a flat `dist/` directory. When false, each goes to `dist/{target}/`.

nsis.description: NSIS installer configurations for this crate.

path.description: Relative path to the crate directory from the project root.

pkgs.description: macOS PKG installer configurations for this crate.

publish.description: Publishing targets (Homebrew, Scoop, AUR, etc.) for this crate.

release.description: GitHub release configuration for this crate.

snapcrafts.description: Snapcraft package configurations for this crate.

universal_binaries.description: macOS universal binary (fat binary) configurations for this crate.

version.description: Pinned semver version. When set, `anodizer bump --strict` refuses to edit this crate's `Cargo.toml` to anything other than this value; without `--strict`, the bump proceeds with a warning. Lets a release captain freeze a crate's version while still running broad `--workspace` bumps.

version_files.description: Repo-committed files that embed this crate's release version outside `Cargo.toml` (repo-root-relative path strings). At `tag` time each file has its occurrences of the old version rewritten to the new version — both bare and `v`-prefixed forms, word-boundary anchored — and is staged into the same bump commit as this crate's `Cargo.toml`. Overrides the workspace-level `defaults.version_files`. An entry may instead be a `path` + `match` mapping scoping the rewrite to the occurrences the `match` regex selects, so several crates can share one file.

version_sync.description: Automatic version number synchronization configuration for this crate.

Defaults.description:
Workspace-level defaults. Each key has the same shape as the matching key under `crates[]` or at the top level, and fills what the config left unset. A field the config sets always keeps its own value.

| Key | Applied to | How |
|---|---|---|
| `builds` | every build of every crate | merged into each `builds[]` entry; a crate with no builds gets one build made from it |
| `archives` | every crate | merged into the crate's archive whose first format matches; appended when none matches; a crate with `archives: false` takes nothing |
| `nfpms`, `snapcrafts`, `flatpaks`, `app_bundles`, `dmgs`, `pkgs`, `msis`, `nsis`, `dockers_v2` | every crate | merged into the crate's entry with the same identity (`id`; `id` then `package_name` for nfpm; `name` for snapcraft); appended when none matches |
| `checksum` | every crate | merged into the crate's `checksum` block |
| `cross` | every crate | used when the crate sets no `cross` |
| `version_files` | every crate | used whole when the crate sets no `version_files`; a crate list is never merged with it |
| `crates.tag_template` | every crate | used when the crate's `tag_template` is unset or empty |
| `publish.<publisher>` | every crate | merged into the crate's `publish.<publisher>` block |
| `publish.on_error`, `publish.on_rollback` | every crate | appended after the crate's own hooks |
| `source`, `notarize`, `srpms` | the top level | merged into the top-level block |
| `upx`, `sign`, `binary_signs`, `docker_signs`, `sbom`, `makeselves`, `install_scripts` | the top level | used as the one entry of the top-level list (`upx`, `signs`, `binary_signs`, `docker_signs`, `sboms`, `makeselfs`, `install_scripts`) when that list is empty |
| `targets` | every build | used by every build that sets no `targets` |
| `env` | the top level | put before the top-level `env`, so a top-level entry with the same key wins |

"Merged" means the default fills every field the entry left unset, nested blocks field by field; a list field the entry sets keeps its own list whole. An empty block (`{}`) in a crate inherits every field. A block or list entry with `skip: true` (or a `skip` string reading `true` or `1`) takes nothing from defaults, and a list default that shares a skipped entry's identity key is not appended; a build's `skip` does not stop the `builds` merge. A list default that matches no entry, including one with no identity key, is appended to the crate's list; an empty or absent list gets it as its one entry.

app_bundles.description: Default app-bundle settings, merged into each crate's app-bundle entry with the same `id`, or appended when none matches.

archives.description: Default archive settings, merged into each crate's archive whose first format matches this block's first format, or appended when none matches. A crate with `archives: false` takes nothing.

binary_signs.description: Default binary-signing settings, used as the one top-level `binary_signs` entry when that list is empty.

builds.description: Default build settings merged into every `crates[].builds[]` entry; a field the build sets keeps its value. A crate with no `builds` gets one build made from this block.

checksum.description: Default checksum settings, merged into every crate's `checksum` block. Same shape as `crates[].checksum`.

crates.description: Per-crate fallbacks for a config with a top-level `crates:` list: `tag_template` is used by every crate whose own `tag_template` is unset or empty. Setting this block without a top-level `crates:` list, or together with `defaults.workspaces`, fails when the config loads.

cross.description: Cross-compilation strategy for every crate that sets no `cross`: auto, zigbuild, cross, or cargo. Same values as `crates[].cross`.

dmgs.description: Default DMG settings, merged into each crate's DMG entry with the same `id`, or appended when none matches.

docker_signs.description: Default Docker image signing settings, used as the one top-level `docker_signs` entry when that list is unset or empty.

dockers_v2.description: Default Docker (V2 API) image settings, merged into each crate's `dockers_v2` entry with the same `id`, or appended when none matches. The `docker_v2:` spelling is still accepted.

env.description: Environment variables (`KEY=VALUE` strings) put before the top-level `env`, so a top-level entry with the same key wins.

flatpaks.description: Default flatpak settings, merged into each crate's flatpak entry with the same `id`, or appended when none matches.

install_scripts.description: Default install-script settings, used as the one top-level `install_scripts` entry when that list is empty.

makeselves.description: Default makeself settings, used as the one top-level `makeselfs` entry when that list is empty.

msis.description: Default MSI settings, merged into each crate's MSI entry with the same `id`, or appended when none matches.

nfpms.description: Default nfpm (deb/rpm/apk) settings, merged into each crate's nfpm entry with the same `id` (or, with no `id`, `package_name`), or appended when none matches.

notarize.description: Default macOS notarization settings, merged into the top-level `notarize` block.

nsis.description: Default NSIS settings, merged into each crate's NSIS entry with the same `id`, or appended when none matches.

pkgs.description: Default macOS PKG settings, merged into each crate's PKG entry with the same `id`, or appended when none matches.

publish.description: Default publisher settings, one block per publisher, each merged into every crate's matching `publish.*` block.

sbom.description: Default SBOM settings, used as the one top-level `sboms` entry when that list is empty.

sign.description: Default artifact signing settings, used as the one top-level `signs` entry when that list is empty.

snapcrafts.description: Default snapcraft settings, merged into each crate's snapcraft entry with the same `name`, or appended when none matches.

source.description: Default source-archive settings, merged into the top-level `source` block.

srpms.description: Default SRPM settings, merged into the top-level `srpms` block.

targets.description: Build targets for every build that sets no `targets` of its own (e.g. `["x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu", "aarch64-apple-darwin"]`). When unset or empty, anodizer's built-in target list applies.

upx.description: Default UPX settings, used as the one top-level `upx` entry when the top-level `upx` list is empty.

version_files.description: Repo-committed files whose embedded release version is rewritten at `tag` time (repo-root-relative path strings). Used whole as the `version_files` of every crate that sets none; a crate's own list replaces it entirely. Takes the same entries as `crates[].version_files`, including the anchored `path` + `match` form.

workspaces.description: Marker for a config with a top-level `workspaces:` list. It holds no fields. Setting it without a top-level `workspaces:` list, or together with `defaults.crates`, fails when the config loads.

DefaultsCrateBlock.description:
Block under `defaults.crates:` that supplies workspace-wide fallbacks for per-crate fields. Also drives the axis-mismatch validator (present only when top-level `crates:` is non-empty).

`deny_unknown_fields` so that typing `defaults.crates: { foo: bar }` fails to parse.

tag_template.description: Git tag template used by every crate whose own `tag_template` is unset or empty. A crate's own non-empty `tag_template` wins. When neither is set, the tag template falls through the rest of the order documented on `crates[].tag_template`.

DefaultsWorkspaceBlock.description:
Marker block under `defaults.workspaces:` that signals workspace-axis defaults scope. It holds no fields; the axis-mismatch validator reads its presence.

`deny_unknown_fields` per the same rationale as `DefaultsCrateBlock`.

author.description: Author name displayed in the embed. Default: `anodizer`.

color.description: Embed color as a decimal integer string (default: "3888754", a blue). Parsed to u32 at runtime. Supports template expressions.

enabled.description: Enable Discord announcements (supports template expressions).

icon_url.description: Icon URL shown beside the embed author; sent only when `author` renders to a name.

message_template.description: Message template for the Discord embed. Default: "{{ ProjectName }} {{ Tag }} is out! Check it out at {{ ReleaseURL }}"

webhook_url.description:
Discord webhook URL.

Prefer `{{ Env.DISCORD_WEBHOOK }}` (or similar) over an in-config literal — plaintext webhook URLs grant full posting access and are NOT redacted from error messages or `dist/config.yaml` after a dry-run / snapshot run.

category_id.description: Category ID to post in (required, must be non-zero).

enabled.description: Enable Discourse announcements (supports template expressions).

message_template.description: Message body template for the forum topic. Default: "{{ ProjectName }} {{ Tag }} is out! Check it out at {{ ReleaseURL }}"

title_template.description: Title template for the forum topic. Default: "{{ ProjectName }} {{ Tag }} is out!"

amd64_variant.description: amd64 microarchitecture variant filter (`v1` / `v2` / `v3` / `v4`), set via the `amd64_variant:` key. When set, only artifacts with the matching `amd64_variant` metadata are included. The legacy `goamd64:` spelling is accepted via serde alias for back-compat with imported configs. When unset, all amd64 variants are included (no filtering). Typed as [`Amd64Variant`], so any value outside `v1`..`v4` is rejected when the config is parsed.

extra_files.description: Additional files to include in the DMG (glob or {glob, name_template}).

id.description: Unique identifier for this DMG config.

ids.description: Build IDs to include. Empty means all builds.

if.description: Template-conditional: skip this DMG config when the gate renders `false`, `0`, `no` or empty (any letter case). Render failure hard-errors (not silent-skip). An absent, empty or blank `if:` imposes no gate and always runs; the falsy test applies to what a non-blank gate renders.

name.description: Output DMG filename (supports templates).

replace.description: Remove source archives from artifacts, keeping only DMG.

skip.description: Skip this DMG config. Accepts bool or template string.

templated_extra_files.description: Extra files whose contents are rendered through the template engine before inclusion. Unlike `extra_files` which copy as-is, template variables like `{{ Tag }}` are expanded. Conditional-skip gate.

use.description: Which artifact type to package: "binary" (default) or "appbundle".

volume_name.description:
Volume label shown in Finder when the image is mounted.

Supports template variables. Defaults to the project name.

DockerDigestConfig.description:
Controls docker image digest file creation.

After each docker image push, a digest file (containing the sha256 digest) is written to the dist directory. This config controls whether that happens and how the files are named.

name_template.description: Template for the digest artifact filename. Default: tag-based naming (e.g., "ghcr.io_owner_app_v1.0.0.digest").

skip.description: Disable docker digest artifact creation when the value is, or a template renders, `true` or `1` (any letter case). Accepts the legacy `disable:` spelling via serde alias for back-compat.

DockerHubConfig.description: Docker Hub description sync configuration. Pushes image descriptions and README content to Docker Hub repositories.

description.description: Short description for the Docker Hub repository (max 100 chars).

full_description.description: Full description (README) source for the Docker Hub repository.

if.description: Template-conditional gate: when the rendered result is falsy (`"false"` / `"0"` / `"no"` / empty), the Docker Hub publisher is skipped. Render failure hard-errors. Exposes the `dockerhub[].if:` conditional gate; distinct from `skip:` (which expresses "always skip") and provides config-import parity. An absent, empty or blank `if:` imposes no gate and always runs; the falsy test applies to what a non-blank gate renders.

images.description: Docker Hub image names to update (e.g. `myorg/myapp`).

required.description:
Override whether this publisher failing should fail the overall release.

Default: `false` — a failure here is logged but does not abort the release. Set to `true` to fail the release on any error.

retain_on_rollback.description: When `true`, a triggered rollback leaves this publisher's work in place and does not try to undo it. Default `false`.

secret_name.description: Environment variable name containing the Docker Hub token.

skip.description: Skip this publisher. Accepts bool or template string. Accepts the legacy `disable:` spelling via serde alias for back-compat with imported configs (the legacy `disable:` spelling).

DockerHubFromFile.description: Read Docker Hub full description content from a local file.

path.description: Path to the file containing the full description.

DockerHubFromUrl.description: Fetch Docker Hub full description content from a URL.

headers.description: Optional HTTP headers for the request. Each value is a template, read as a credential: trimmed, and a value that fails to render stops the run with an error naming its header.

url.description: URL to fetch the full description from.

DockerHubFullDescription.description: Full description source for Docker Hub: either from a URL or a local file.

from_file.description: Read full description content from a local file.

from_url.description: Fetch full description content from a URL.

DockerManifestConfig.description: Deprecated: prefer `dockers_v2`, which produces multi-arch manifests from its `platforms:` field. `docker_manifests` is kept so imported configs still load, and for stitching together manifest lists from images that were not built by `dockers_v2` in the same run.

id.description: Unique identifier for this manifest config.

image_templates.description: Image references to include in the manifest.

name_template.description: Template for the manifest name, e.g. "ghcr.io/owner/app:{{ Version }}".

retry.description: Retry configuration for manifest push (handles transient registry errors).

skip_push.description:
Skip push: `true`, `false`, `"auto"` (skip for prereleases), or a template rendered at run time. The words `true`, `false`, `1`, `0` and `auto` load in any letter case, quoted or unquoted; any other string is a template.

```yaml
skip_push: "{{ IsSnapshot }}"
```

use.description: Docker backend for manifest commands: `"docker"` (default) or `"podman"`; any other value (including `"buildx"`) fails the docker stage. The `"podman"` backend is **Linux-only**: on a macOS or Windows host the docker stage fails before any `podman` command runs. `check config` does not check the host.

DockerRetryConfig.description:
Per-pipe retry configuration for `docker.retry` / `docker_manifest.retry`.

**Deprecated**: prefer the top-level `retry:` block ([`super::RetryConfig`]) which applies to docker pipes (and every other network-bound stage) via `Project.Retry`. When a per-pipe block is present alongside the top-level block, the per-pipe values win for back-compat, but `stage-docker::resolve_retry_params` emits a one-shot deprecation warning. New configs should leave this field unset.

attempts.description: Number of retry attempts for failed docker push operations (default: 10, set in `crates/stage-docker/src/lib.rs::resolve_retry_settings`).

delay.description: Duration string for the initial retry delay (default: `"10s"`), in the duration format every config field uses, at most one year. A bare number is read as seconds. Examples: `"1s"`, `"500ms"`, `"10"`.

max_delay.description: Maximum delay between retries (default: `"5m"`), in the same format as `delay`. Caps the exponential backoff so attempt-9 with a 10s base does not stretch to ~42 min. Example: `"30s"`.

args.description: Arguments passed to the signing command. `{{ .Artifact }}` is replaced by the image reference with its digest and `{{ .Signature }}` by the synthesized `<image>@<digest>.sig` name before the rest is rendered as a template; `{{ .Digest }}` renders the image digest. Shell variables such as `${artifact}` are never expanded on the docker path and reach the signing command as literal text.

artifacts.description: Which docker artifacts to sign: `all`, `images`, `manifests`, `none`, or empty. Empty is the default and signs the canonical docker images. The singular `image` and `manifest` are refused: the sign stage fails the run, so a misspelled filter cannot sign nothing in silence.

certificate.description: Certificate file whose PRESENCE selects cosign's bundle verification mode. The path itself never reaches the signing command: `{{ .Certificate }}` in `args:` renders empty on the docker path.

env.description: Environment variables passed to the signing command.

id.description: Unique identifier for this docker sign config.

ids.description: Docker config IDs filter: only sign images from configs whose `id` is in this list.

if.description: Template-conditional: skip this docker sign config when the gate renders `false`, `0`, `no` or empty (any letter case). An absent, empty or blank `if:` imposes no gate and always runs; the falsy test applies to what a non-blank gate renders.

output.description: Capture and log stdout/stderr of the docker signing command.

signature.description: Ignored. A container signature is stored in the registry beside the image, and no file is written, so the docker sign stage synthesizes the `<image>@<digest>.sig` name its argv substitutes and reads this template nowhere.

stdin.description: Content written to the signing command's stdin. Rendered as a template with nothing substituted first, so neither `{{ .Artifact }}` nor `${artifact}` names anything here. The rendered value is a credential: leading and trailing whitespace is removed, and a template that does not render is an error naming `docker_signs[<id>].stdin` without the template's text.

stdin_file.description: Path to a file whose content is written to the signing command's stdin.

verify.description: Verification of each signature after signing. Docker signatures are verified with `cosign verify` against the registry the signature was just pushed to.

DockerV2Config.description:
Docker V2 configuration — the canonical Docker build API.

Notable fields:
- `images` + `tags`, two lists that together name every pushed reference
- `annotations` map for OCI annotations (`--annotation`)
- `build_args` map for build-time variables
- `skip` as a bool or a template for conditional opt-out
- `sbom` as a bool or a template; when `true` or `1`, adds `--attest=type=sbom` to buildx
- `flags` for arbitrary extra `docker build` flags
- `platforms` is the only target selector — no per-arch field overrides

annotations.description:
OCI annotations to apply via `--annotation key=value` flags.

On a multi-platform build a key is written to the image index (`index:key=value`) unless it already names a buildx scope: a comma-separated list of `index`, `manifest`, `index-descriptor` and `manifest-descriptor`, each optionally platform-qualified, as in `manifest:key`, `index,manifest:key` or `manifest[linux/amd64]:key`. A prefix holding any other entry is part of the key and is scoped to the index too. A single-platform build passes every key as written.

build_args.description:
Build arguments passed as `--build-arg KEY=VALUE`.

Each value is template-expanded and forwarded verbatim to buildx (one argv token per pair, no shell tokenization). Prefer `{{ Env.VAR }}` over raw user-config strings for secrets — buildx records build-args in image history by default, so plaintext values here propagate into the image metadata.

A key naming a global `ARG` (one declared before the first `FROM`) also replaces that `ARG`'s default when resolving the base image behind `{{ BaseImage }}` and `{{ BaseImageDigest }}`, when its value renders non-empty. Build args render before the base image resolves, so they cannot reference `{{ BaseImage }}` themselves.

dockerfile.description: Path to the Dockerfile relative to the project root.

extra_files.description: Extra files to copy into the Docker build context.

flags.description: Arbitrary extra flags passed to the docker build command.

hooks.description:
Pre/post hooks for this dockers_v2 config. Each hook accepts the same `cmd`/`dir`/`env`/`output` shape as build/archive hooks. `pre` hooks run after the staging directory is prepared but before `docker buildx build`; `post` hooks run after the image digest is captured. Hook commands, working directories, and env values are template-expanded; in addition to the standard template variables, hooks see:

- `{{ Images }}` — list of `image:tag` references for this build. Iterate via `{% for img in Images %}{{ img }}{% endfor %}` to mirror a list exposure of the same field; `{{ Images | join(sep=",") }}` reproduces a flat comma-separated string for legacy templates.
- `{{ Dockerfile }}` — path to the rendered Dockerfile
- `{{ ContextDir }}` — path to the buildx context staging directory
- `{{ Digest }}` — the digest the registry stores for the build (post hooks only): the image manifest single-platform, the image index multi-platform. Read from buildx's `--metadata-file` (`containerimage.digest`), or from `podman push --digestfile` under `use: podman`. A build that exports no image has no digest, and a post hook that needs one then fails the build
- `{{ BaseImage }}` / `{{ BaseImageDigest }}` — final-stage base image (the `BaseImage` / `BaseImageDigest` overlay)

id.description: Unique identifier for this Docker V2 config.

ids.description: Build IDs filter: only include binary artifacts whose metadata `id` is in this list.

images.description: Base image names (e.g., ["ghcr.io/owner/app"]). Combined with `tags` to form full references.

labels.description: OCI labels to apply to the image via `--label key=value` flags.

oci_labels.description: Auto-inject the standard predefined `org.opencontainers.image.*` labels (created, source, revision, version, title, description, licenses, url, documentation, vendor), derived from project/git/Cargo context. Default ON; set `oci_labels: false` to opt out. Each auto-label is emitted only when its value is derivable, and any key the user also supplies in `labels:` wins (the auto value never clobbers an explicit user label). `created` is derived from `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` for byte-reproducibility (never wall-clock) and is omitted when no reproducible source date is resolvable.

retry.description: Retry configuration for docker push operations.

sbom.description: Adds `--attest=type=sbom` to the buildx build when the value is, or a template renders, `true` or `1` (any letter case). Default: `true`. A snapshot run never adds it.

skip.description: Skip this docker build entirely when the value is, or a template renders, `true` or `1` (any letter case). Accepts the legacy `disable:` spelling via serde alias for back-compat.

tags.description: Tag suffixes (e.g., ["latest", "{{ Version }}"]). Each image is tagged with each tag.

use.description:
Docker backend for build commands: `"buildx"` (default) or `"podman"`.

The default `"buildx"` invokes `docker buildx build` with the full set of BuildKit features (multi-platform, attestations, `--rewrite-timestamp`, SBOM, OCI exporter). Setting `use: podman` swaps the binary to `podman build` and drops every buildx-only flag. The docker stage fails an entry that combines `use: podman` with `sbom` reading true outside a snapshot (`sbom` defaults to `true`, so set `sbom: false`), or with a `--rewrite-timestamp`, `--sbom`, `--provenance`, `--attest`, `--output`, `--cache-from` or `--cache-to` flag, because plain podman does not recognise them. Any value other than `buildx` or `podman` fails the same way.

**Linux-only.** On a macOS or Windows host the docker stage fails an entry with `use: podman` with an error naming the entry, before any `podman` command runs. `check config` does not check the host.

enabled.description: Enable email announcements (supports template expressions).

encryption.description: Transport encryption mode. `auto` (the default) picks SMTPS for port 465, plain SMTP for port 25, and STARTTLS for everything else; `tls` forces SMTPS, `starttls` forces STARTTLS, `none` forces plain SMTP.

host.description: SMTP server hostname. When set, uses SMTP transport. When absent, falls back to sendmail/msmtp.

port.description:
SMTP server port (default: 587 for STARTTLS).

Anodizer-additive UX win (locked 2026-04-28): an unset SMTP `port` would otherwise be an error when it is unset (zero value). Anodizer defaults to 587 — the IETF submission port — so the common case (corporate / SaaS SMTP relays exposing STARTTLS on 587) works out of the box without a config knob. The `auto` encryption mode then resolves to STARTTLS for 587, which is the conventional pairing. Pinned by `test_email_smtp_port_defaults_to_587`.

subject_template.description: Email subject template. Default: "{{ ProjectName }} {{ Tag }} is out!"

username.description: SMTP username (can also be set via SMTP_USERNAME env var).

oneOf.description: Pick based on port: 465 → SMTPS, 25 → none, otherwise STARTTLS.
Implicit TLS on connect (typically port 465).
Plain SMTP that upgrades to TLS via STARTTLS (typically port 587).
Plain SMTP, no TLS. Only safe on trusted local relays (port 25).

EnvFilesConfig.description:
Environment file configuration.

Accepts two forms:
- **List form** (anodizer extension): array of `.env` file paths loaded as KEY=VALUE.

  ```yaml
  env_files:
    - .env
    - .release.env
  ```

- **Struct form**: paths to files containing provider tokens.

  ```yaml
  env_files:
    github_token: ~/.config/goreleaser/github_token
    gitlab_token: ~/.config/goreleaser/gitlab_token
    gitea_token: ~/.config/goreleaser/gitea_token
  ```

anyOf.description: List of `.env` file paths to load (KEY=VALUE format).

EnvFilesTokenConfig.description:
Structured token file paths for provider authentication.

Each field points to a file containing a single-line token. When present, the file is read and the corresponding environment variable is set (e.g., `github_token` file -> `GITHUB_TOKEN` env var).

Token-file path overrides.

gitea_token.description: Path to file containing the Gitea token. Default: `~/.config/goreleaser/gitea_token`.

github_token.description: Path to file containing the GitHub token. Default: `~/.config/goreleaser/github_token`.

gitlab_token.description: Path to file containing the GitLab token. Default: `~/.config/goreleaser/gitlab_token`.

ExtraFileSpec.description:
Specifies an extra file to include in checksums or release uploads. Can be a simple glob string or a detailed object with glob and name_template fields.

See [`ArchiveFileSpec`] doc comment for why this is a separate type.

allow_empty.description: When true, treat a glob that matches zero files as a no-op. When false, it is a hard error. Useful for assets produced only in CI (e.g. signing public keys derived from a secret) that must not break local snapshot/dry-run flows. Defaults to false, matching the prior fail-fast behavior.

name_template.description: Optional override for the upload filename.

FileInfo.description: Shared file metadata (owner, group, mode, mtime) used by both archive entries and nFPM package contents. Previously duplicated as `ArchiveFileInfo` and `NfpmFileInfo`; now unified.

mode.description: File permission mode. Accepts a YAML int (decimal, e.g. `420` for `0o644`) or an octal-prefixed string (`"0o644"`, `"0644"`). This a `uint32` type for `Mode` on archive/nfpm contents while letting users spell octal naturally in YAML.

mtime.description: File modification time in RFC3339 format (e.g., "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z").

app_id.description: Flatpak application ID in reverse-DNS notation (e.g. org.example.MyApp). Required.

command.description: Command to run inside the Flatpak sandbox. Defaults to first binary name.

extra_files.description: Additional files to include alongside the binary (glob or {glob, name_template}).

id.description: Unique identifier for this Flatpak config.

ids.description: Build IDs to include. Empty means all builds.

replace.description: Remove source archives from artifacts, keeping only the Flatpak bundle.

skip.description: Skip this Flatpak config. Accepts bool or template string. Accepts the legacy `disable:` spelling via serde alias for back-compat.

ForceTokenKind.description: Which SCM token to force for authentication, overriding automatic detection.

formats.description: Plural format overrides for this OS: tar.gz, tar.xz, tar.zst, tar, zip, gz, xz, or binary.

os.description: Operating system this override applies to (e.g., "windows", "darwin", "linux").

GemFuryConfig.description:
Gemfury package registry publisher configuration.

Pushes deb / rpm / apk artifacts to `https://push.fury.io/<account>`. Authenticates via HTTP Basic auth using the push token as the username (empty password) — the conventional Fury push form.

account.description: Gemfury account name. Required; rendered through the template engine so `account: "{{ Env.MY_FURY_ACCOUNT }}"` works.

api_secret_name.description: Environment variable name carrying the API (delete) token. Default `FURY_API_TOKEN`.

api_token.description: Optional API token used by rollback to issue `DELETE /<account>/packages/<name>/versions/<version>`. When unset, the env var named by `api_secret_name` (default `FURY_API_TOKEN`) is consulted at rollback time. If both are absent at rollback time, the publisher falls back to a manual-cleanup warn.

exclude.description:
Glob patterns matched against each artifact's file name; anodizer drops any artifact whose name matches at least one glob from THIS Gemfury target only. Use it to keep heavy sidecars off the account while packages still upload. Composes with `ids:` and the format filter (all filters apply). Unset or empty keeps everything.

```yaml
gemfury:
  - account: my-account
    exclude: ["*.sha256", "*.sig", "*.cdx.json"]
```

formats.description: Package format filter: only push artifacts matching these formats. Defaults to `["apk", "deb", "rpm"]`.

id.description: Unique identifier for selecting this entry from the CLI (`--id=...`).

ids.description: Build IDs filter: only include artifacts whose archive `id` is in this list.

if.description: Template-conditional gate: when the rendered result is falsy (`"false"` / `"0"` / `"no"` / empty), the Gemfury publisher entry is skipped. Render failure hard-errors. Exposes the `gemfury[].if:` conditional gate; distinct from `skip:` (which expresses "always skip") and provides config-import parity. An absent, empty or blank `if:` imposes no gate and always runs; the falsy test applies to what a non-blank gate renders.

required.description:
Override whether this publisher failing should fail the overall release.

Default: `true` — Gemfury is a Manager-group publisher (mutable but reversible via the delete API), so a failed publish aborts by default to avoid surprising the operator with a half-released version. Set to `false` to log failures but continue.

retain_on_rollback.description: When `true`, a triggered rollback leaves this publisher's work in place and does not try to undo it. Default `false`.

secret_name.description: Environment variable name carrying the push token. Default `FURY_PUSH_TOKEN`. The actual token VALUE is read from this env var at publish/rollback time.

skip.description: Template-conditional skip: skip this publisher entry when the value is, or a template renders, `true` or `1` (any letter case). Accepts bool or template string. Accepts the legacy `disable:` spelling via serde alias for back-compat with imported `gemfury[].disable:` configs.

token.description: Push token used as the HTTP Basic auth username (empty password). When unset, the env var named by `secret_name` (default `FURY_PUSH_TOKEN`) is consulted at publish time. NEVER logged.

GitConfig.description:
Git-level tag discovery and sorting settings.

Controls how anodizer discovers and orders tags when determining the current and previous versions. Version *bumping* is set in the separate `tag:` block.

ignore_tag_prefixes.description: Tag prefixes to ignore during version detection (supports templates). Tags starting with any prefix in this list are excluded. The ignore-tag-prefixes feature.

ignore_tags.description: Tag patterns to ignore during version detection (supports templates). Tags matching any pattern in this list are excluded from version detection entirely.

prerelease_suffix.description: Suffix that identifies pre-release tags for sorting purposes. When set, tags ending with this suffix are treated as pre-releases and sorted accordingly during tag discovery.

tag_sort.description:
How to sort git tags when determining the latest version.

Accepted values:
- `"-version:refname"` (default) — lexicographic version sort on the tag name.
- `"-version:creatordate"` — sort by the tag's creation date (newest first).
- `"semver"` — strict SemVer 2.0.0 ordering computed in Rust; prereleases sort below their release per spec section 11. Bypasses git's native sort.
- `"smartsemver"` — same ordering as `"semver"`, but when the current version (resolved from the template `Version` variable) is non-prerelease, prerelease tags are filtered out before previous-tag selection. Prevents `v0.2.0-beta.3` from being picked as the predecessor of `v0.2.0` (which would otherwise produce an empty changelog).

HomebrewCaskBinary.description:
Cask `binary` stanza entry.

Two shapes accepted in YAML:
- bare string — `"my-cli"` → renders `binary "my-cli"`.
- `{ name, target }` object — `{ name: "my-cli", target: "mycli" }` → renders `binary "my-cli", target: "mycli"`. The `target:` form is the Homebrew Ruby cask DSL rename: install the symlink at `/usr/local/bin/<target>` in place of `/usr/local/bin/<name>`.

anyOf.description: Bare binary name. Equivalent to `{ name: "<n>", target: None }`.

name.description: Path inside the .app bundle (e.g. `"my-cli"`).

target.description: Optional rename target — the symlink name in `/usr/local/bin`. When unset, the symlink uses `name`.

HomebrewCaskCompletions.description: Shell completion file paths for Homebrew Cask.

HomebrewCaskConfig.description:
Homebrew Cask configuration, with the same keys in two places:
- `homebrew_casks:`: a top-level list; carries `repository`, `commit_author`, `directory`, `ids`, `url`, structured `uninstall`/`zap`, etc.
- `crates[].publish.homebrew_cask:`: a per-crate cask, where `url_template` is the simpler alternative to `url`.

Every key is optional in both places.

binaries.description:
Binary stubs to create in /usr/local/bin.

Each entry is either a bare string (`"my-cli"` → emits `binary "my-cli"`) or a structured `{ name, target }` object (`{ name: "my-cli", target: "mycli" }` → emits `binary "my-cli", target: "mycli"`). The `target:` form mirrors the Homebrew Ruby cask DSL for binary renames — without it, a wrapped binary installs at the wrong path. Cask binary entry.

binary.description: Deprecated singular spelling of [`Self::binaries`]. The upstream replaced `binary: foo` with `binaries: [foo]`; this field captures the legacy spelling so imported configs keep parsing. [`apply_homebrew_cask_legacy_singulars`](super::super::apply_homebrew_cask_legacy_singulars) folds the value into [`Self::binaries`] at config-load time and emits a one-time deprecation warning per occurrence. The field is excluded from serialization so a round-tripped config emits only the canonical plural form.

commit_msg_template.description: Custom commit message template. Default: "Brew cask update for {{ ProjectName }} version {{ Tag }}"

custom_block.description: Arbitrary Ruby code inserted into the cask block.

dependencies.description: Cask dependencies (other casks or formulae). Rendered casks first, then formulae, each group sorted by name without regard to case with the names written as given, the order `brew style` requires.

depends_on_macos.description:
Whether the cask renders `depends_on :macos`. When unset, anodizer decides from the downloads and the `custom_block`: a cask with no Linux download gets `depends_on :macos` unless its `custom_block` gives it a Linux side or declares an OS dependency.

The block is read as code, with these set aside, each one carrying on into the next lines until it closes: `"…"`, `'…'` and `` `…` `` strings (inside `"…"` and `` `…` ``, `#{…}` is read as code, so the string ends at its own quote, and `#$"` interpolates `$"`); heredoc bodies (`<<~TAG`, `<<-TAG`, `<<TAG`, a `<<` before a space or a digit being a shift; unless the tag is single-quoted, a body line ending in an odd run of `\` joins the next one, so a tag there does not close it, and `#{…}` in a body line is code, so a heredoc opened there has its body read from the next line, before the rest of the body around it, and a `#{…}` left open at the end of a body line reads on into the next); `%()`, `%q`, `%Q`, `%w`, `%W`, `%i`, `%I`, `%r`, `%s` and `%x` literals delimited by nesting brackets or one repeated punctuation character, a typed one also by a space or the end of the line (a list, `%w` `%W` `%i` `%I`, splits its words on whitespace, so whitespace never closes it), and a bare `%` where an operand must stand (with nothing before it on its statement but an operator, or after a label `a:`, the `:` of a ternary or a keyword that takes an operand: `and`, `begin`, `break`, `case`, `do`, `else`, `elsif`, `ensure`, `if`, `in`, `next`, `or`, `rescue`, `return`, `then`, `unless`, `until`, `when` or `while`) also by a space, a tab, `=` or the end of the line (a literal delimited by the end of its line holds the next line, and the one after while the held line ends in an odd run of `\`, and a `%r` closed that way takes the letters that start the line after as its options); `?x` character literals (not `?ab`, nor `?"a"` after a word that may be a local); a `/…/` regex where an operand stands; `#` comments; and `=begin` … `=end` comments, opened on any line that starts in code, the code of a `#{…}` left open at the end of the line before included. The code inside `#{…}` is kept apart from the code around it, in every literal that interpolates (`"…"` and `` `…` `` strings, `:"…"` symbols, heredocs whose tag is not single-quoted, `%()`, `%Q`, `%W`, `%I`, `%r` and `%x` literals and `/…/` regexes), and each `#{…}` is read as statements of its own: its words count toward the Linux side, a `depends_on` opening one of its statements toward the OS dependency, and a `;` in it ends no statement around the literal; it is read in the scopes around the literal by the rules below, as Ruby reads it, so the names it assigns are locals after it and the parameters and locals of a block, lambda or `def` inside it end with that block, lambda or `def` (`"#{on_linux}"` names a Linux side, `'#{on_linux}'` does not). None opens after a `:` that makes a symbol (one written against a method call that heads its statement or follows `.`, `&.` or `::` does, as in `` foo:` ``, since such a call takes no label), in a special global (`$"`), or where it names a method: after `.`, `&.` or `::` (with or without a space, whatever the name looks like, so `x. %` and `a&.!~` are method names) or `def`, and as the `?` or `!` of a method name. Straight after a name Ruby reads as a method call, a `?` opens a character literal (`EOS!?"`, `foo?=`, `x&.def??"`, `foo.nil?=`). Ruby reads a name as a method call after `.`, `&.` or `::`, whatever it spells, and elsewhere unless it is a local variable, a parameter, a number, a variable with a sigil, or `self`, `nil`, `true`, `false`, `end`, `__FILE__`, `__LINE__` or `__ENCODING__`. A `?` or `!` read as an operator ends no word, so a `/` after it opens a regex (`!/a/`).

A `<<`, `%`, `?` or `/` after a value is a shift, a modulo, a ternary or a division: after `)`, `]`, `}`, a number, a literal, a symbol (the operator ones and `:a=`, `:a?`, `:a!` included), `self`, `nil`, `true`, `false`, `end`, `class`, `def`, an `@` or `$` variable, a local assigned earlier in its scope (`name =`, `name ||=` and the other operator assignments wherever they stand, as in `f(b += 1)`, unless the target follows `.`, `&.` or `::` or has a sigil, `a, b =`, `a, (b, c) =`, `(a, b) =`, `a, =`, `for a in`, `rescue => a`, a named group before `=~` in a regex with no `#{…}`, a name in an `in` pattern, the target of a rightward `=>`), a parameter of a block (`|a, b; c|`, also over several lines), method (`def name(a, b = 1)`, with or without parentheses; a setter `def name=(v)` binds `v` alone) or lambda (`->(x)`, `-> (x)`), or a word other than a keyword written straight against a `<<`, `%` or `/`. A `def` body sees none of the locals outside it; a block, a lambda body (`-> { … }`) included, sees them, and its parameters and the locals first assigned in it end at its `end` or `}`; `if`, `while`, `case` and `begin` open no scope. A statement continued with a `\` at the end of a line, with a `?\` character literal holding the newline, with a `.`, `&.` or `::` that ends a line (past blank and comment lines) or with a literal the newline closes, is read as one statement, so the code before the break decides what the operator, `if` or `until` after it is. After a word, a `/` followed by a space or `=` divides, and a `:` after a value ends a ternary and starts no symbol, so an operand stands after it. The word after a `::` is a constant path or a method, also when the `::` ended an earlier line. After an operator, `(`, `,`, `;`, the start of a line, a label, a Ruby keyword, any method of the cask DSL, a common method such as `puts` or a name ending in `?` or `!` followed by a space (no local or parameter is spelled that way) the operator opens a literal, and after any other word followed by a space it is read as an opener too, which is a guess.

A Linux side is the word `on_linux`, `on_system` or `app_image` in that code. An OS dependency is a statement whose first word is `depends_on` (at the start of a line or after a `;`, in the code around the literals or in a `#{…}`, after any opening `(`) that names the key `macos:`, `maximum_macos:` or `linux:`, or the symbol `:macos` or `:linux`; the statement continues onto the next line while a line ends with `,`, `(`, `[`, `{`, `|`, `.`, `&&`, `||`, `=>` or `\`, ends inside an open literal, or while it has opened more `(`, `[` and `{` than it closed.

The checks fall back to a word scan of the raw text, comments and strings included, which may over-match, when a literal is still open after the last line, when a guess opens a literal that spans several lines, or when a parameter still in scope is followed by a `<<` whose heredoc tag closes on a later line. A word scan that finds a Linux-side word leaves `depends_on :macos` out and moves a flat download into `on_macos`, one that finds a `depends_on` OS key leaves the bare dependency out, and one that finds neither adds `depends_on :macos`; the render warns once per command unless this field is set.

Read wrongly with no warning: a stanza built at runtime (through `send` or `define_method`), a `depends_on` after a `do` on the same line, and a guess whose literal closes on the same line, whose content is set aside.

`true` renders `depends_on :macos` with a flat download; `false` renders no dependency and places a flat download inside `on_macos`.

description.description: Cask description.

directory.description: Subdirectory in the tap repo for cask placement (default: "Casks").

generate_completions_from_executable.description: Auto-generate shell completions from an executable.

ids.description: Build IDs filter: only include artifacts from builds whose `id` is in this list.

if.description: Template-conditional gate: when the rendered result is falsy (`"false"` / `"0"` / `"no"` / empty), the Homebrew Cask config is skipped. Render failure hard-errors. Config key: `homebrew_casks[].if:`. An absent, empty or blank `if:` imposes no gate and always runs; the falsy test applies to what a non-blank gate renders.

livecheck.description: `livecheck` stanza configuration for the cask. When unset, the cask emits `livecheck do\n  skip "Auto-generated on release."\nend` (a binary cask's download URL/sha256 are rewritten on every release, so `brew livecheck` has nothing stable to poll). Setting any of `strategy:`, `url:` or `regex:` turns on active version detection, unless `skip: true` is also set. Reuses the formula `livecheck` config type; an active cask livecheck with no `url:` reads `url :url`.

manpage.description: Deprecated singular spelling of [`Self::manpages`]. The upstream replaced `manpage: foo.1` with `manpages: [foo.1]`; this field captures the legacy spelling so imported configs keep parsing. [`apply_homebrew_cask_legacy_singulars`](super::super::apply_homebrew_cask_legacy_singulars) folds the value into [`Self::manpages`] at config-load time and emits a one-time deprecation warning per occurrence. The field is excluded from serialization so a round-tripped config emits only the canonical plural form.

name.description: Cask name (default: crate / project name).

repository.description: Unified repository config for the Homebrew tap.

required.description:
Override whether this publisher failing should fail the overall release.

Default: `false` — a failure here is logged but does not abort the release. Set to `true` to fail the release on any error.

retain_on_rollback.description: When `true`, a triggered rollback leaves this publisher's work in place and does not try to undo it. Default `false`.

service.description: Path of a macOS Services bundle (for example `MyTool.workflow`) inside the download, written as `service "<path>"`.

skip_upload.description: Skip publishing the cask. `"true"` always skips; `"auto"` skips for prerelease versions. Accepts bool or template string.

update_existing_pr.description: When true, force-push the updated cask file to the existing PR branch when a PR for the same head branch already exists. The PR content is updated in place, so no duplicate is created. When false (default), the push is skipped and a warning is emitted so the operator sees that the publisher did not update the PR.

url_template.description:
Simple URL template for the .dmg/.zip download (per-crate shorthand).

Cannot be combined with `url.template:` — set one or the other. If both are present, config validation rejects the config at parse time. Use `url:` for the structured form (verified domain, custom headers, etc.) or `url_template:` for a bare string shorthand — never both simultaneously.

verified.description: **Deprecated.** Verification string (domain shown to user). Homebrew removed the `verified:` stanza (Homebrew/brew#23280) and now applies its default URL verification, so anodizer no longer writes it into the cask. The field still parses so existing configs keep loading, and a deprecation warning names it at config-load time.

commit_msg_template.description: Custom commit message template. Rendered via Tera with the standard release template variables (`ProjectName`, `Tag`, `Version`, etc.). Default: `"Brew formula update for {{ ProjectName }} version {{ Tag }}"`.

Renders the modern homebrew-core idiom `generate_completions_from_executable(bin/"<exe>", ...)` in the install block. Preferred over `completions` when the binary can emit its own completions; the two are independent and may both be set.

homepage.description: Project homepage URL. Falls back to the GitHub release URL when unset.

Config key: `brews[].if:`. An absent, empty or blank `if:` imposes no gate and always runs; the falsy test applies to what a non-blank gate renders.

When unset, a binary tap formula emits `livecheck { skip "Auto-generated on release." }` to match the cask (the archive URL/sha are rewritten on every release, so `brew livecheck` cannot meaningfully poll). Set `strategy:` / `regex:`/`url:` to opt into active version detection instead.

Each entry renders a `man1.install "<path>"` line in the install block, mirroring real Rust-CLI formulae (ripgrep, fd, bat). A path ending in `.N` (where N is 1–8) routes to the matching `manN` section; anything else defaults to `man1`.

name.description: Override the formula name (default: crate name).

post_install.description: Post-install commands (separate `def post_install` block in formula).

repository.description: The tap repository: owner and name, plus branch, token, pull request and git SSH settings. Replaces the older `tap:` key, which took only an owner and a name and is no longer accepted.

required.description:
Override whether this publisher failing should fail the overall release.

Default: `false` — a failure here is logged but does not abort the release. Set to `true` to fail the release on any error.

retain_on_rollback.description: When `true`, a triggered rollback leaves this publisher's work in place and does not try to undo it. Default `false`.

service.description: Homebrew service block content (alternative to plist).

skip_upload.description: Skip publishing the formula.  `"true"` always skips; `"auto"` skips for prerelease versions. Accepts bool or template string.

test.description: Ruby `test` block content for the formula (run by `brew test`).

url_headers.description: HTTP headers to include in download requests (e.g. for private repos).

url_template.description: Custom URL template for download URLs (overrides release URL).

HomebrewConflict.description: A Homebrew conflict entry, supporting both a bare name string and a structured object with an optional `because` reason.

anyOf.description: Name with reason (e.g. `{name: "other-tool", because: "both install a bin/foo binary"}`).

HomebrewCoreConfig.description:
homebrew-core formula-bump publisher configuration.

Bumps an EXISTING formula in `Homebrew/homebrew-core` (or any formula repository override) purely through the GitHub API — no clone, no `brew` invocation. The formula file's `url` (or `tag:`/`revision:` pair), `sha256`, and `version` stanzas are rewritten to the new release, the change is committed to a branch, and a pull request is opened against the formula repository. Each `homebrew_cores[]` entry bumps one formula.

Every field is optional: the formula name defaults to the crate name, the target repository defaults to `Homebrew/homebrew-core`, the formula path defaults to the sharded core layout (`Formula/<letter>/<name>.rb`, falling back to the flat `Formula/<name>.rb`), and the download URL defaults to the GitHub source tarball for the release tag.

```yaml
homebrew_cores:
  - name: my-tool
```

commit_author.description:
Commit author for the formula-bump commit, with optional signing. Its `use_github_app_token` is the canonical homebrew-core knob: when set, the `author`/`committer` fields are omitted from the contents-API commit so GitHub attributes it to the token's own account — the `<app-slug>[bot]` identity a GitHub App workflow needs to satisfy homebrew-core's DCO/CLA policy. Otherwise the resolved `name`/`email` (config → local git identity → the anodizer default) author the commit.

Note: `signing` has no effect here — formula bumps commit through the GitHub contents API, which GitHub signs server-side; the git `-c commit.gpgsign` path the tap/winget/krew publishers use does not apply.

```yaml
homebrew_cores:
  - commit_author:
      use_github_app_token: true
```

commit_msg_template.description: Templated commit message (also the PR title). Default: `"<formula> <version>"` — the message form homebrew-core's CI expects for version bumps.

direct_commit.description:
Commit straight to the base branch and open no pull request. Accepts bool or template string. Only honored for formula repositories you can push to — bumps targeting `Homebrew/homebrew-core` always go through a fork + PR, because homebrew-core never accepts direct pushes.

A back-compat alias for `repository.pull_request.enabled: false`, the preferred spelling shared with the tap/scoop/nix publishers — either one selects the direct-commit path (both are still overridden by the always-fork-and-PR rule for `Homebrew/homebrew-core`).

download_url.description: Templated download URL written into the formula's `url` stanza. Defaults to the GitHub source tarball for the release tag: `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/archive/refs/tags/<tag>.tar.gz` (owner/repo derived from the crate's release repository, then the git remote).

id.description: Unique identifier for selecting this entry from the CLI (`--id=...`).

ids.description: Crate scoping: when set, the formula `name` default is derived from the first crate named here. Unset, it comes from the workspace's primary crate. The workspace per-crate pattern — one `homebrew_cores[]` entry per crate, each scoped by `ids:`.

if.description: Template-conditional gate: when the rendered result is falsy (`"false"` / `"0"` / `"no"` / empty), this entry is skipped. Render failure hard-errors. An absent, empty or blank `if:` imposes no gate and always runs; the falsy test applies to what a non-blank gate renders.

name.description: Formula name (templated). Defaults to the scoped crate name (see `ids:`), then the workspace's primary crate name, then the project name.

path.description: Formula file path inside the repository (templated). Defaults to the homebrew-core sharded layout `Formula/<first-letter>/<name>.rb`, falling back to the flat `Formula/<name>.rb` used by most personal taps when the sharded path does not exist.

repository.description:
Target formula repository. Defaults to `Homebrew/homebrew-core`. Carries the auth token override (`repository.token`), the base branch (`repository.branch`, default: the repo's default branch), and PR settings (`repository.pull_request.draft` / `.body`).

```yaml
homebrew_cores:
  - repository: { owner: my-org, name: my-formulas }
```

required.description:
Override whether this publisher failing should fail the overall release.

Default: `false` — the bump is a PR that can be re-opened by hand, so a failure here is logged but does not abort the release. Set to `true` to fail the release on any error.

retain_on_rollback.description: When `true`, a triggered rollback leaves the opened pull request in place and does not close it. Default `false`.

sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 of the new download (templated). When unset, anodizer downloads `download_url` and hashes it — the same behavior as `brew bump-formula-pr` without `--sha256`.

skip.description: Skip this publisher. Accepts bool or template string. Accepts the legacy `disable:` spelling via serde alias for back-compat.

update_existing_pr.description: When `true` or `1`, refresh the existing bump PR in place: a same-version re-cut force-resets the bump branch to the current base and re-commits the rewritten formula, so the open PR carries this run's content and no duplicate PR is opened. When `false`, `0` or empty (default), an already-open bump PR is left untouched and a warning names this toggle. Accepts bool or template string. Mirrors `winget` / `krew` / `homebrew_cask`'s `update_existing_pr`.

name.description: Homebrew formula name of the dependency. The formula lists its dependencies by type (`build`, `test`, runtime, `recommended`, `optional`) and within a type by name without regard to case, the order `brew style` requires; the names are written as given.

os.description: Restrict to a specific OS: `"mac"` or `"linux"`.

type.description: Dependency type, rendered as `depends_on "name" => :type`: `"build"`, `"test"`, `"recommended"` or `"optional"`. Takes precedence over `version`.

HomebrewLivecheck.description:
`livecheck` stanza configuration for a Homebrew formula or cask.

Default (the struct absent from config): the formula emits a `livecheck { skip "Auto-generated on release." }` block — correct for a binary tap whose archive URL/sha256 are rewritten every release. Setting any of `strategy`, `url` or `regex` turns on active version polling:

```yaml
livecheck:
  strategy: github_latest
```

renders:

```ruby
livecheck do
  url :stable
  strategy :github_latest
end
```

regex.description: `regex(...)` argument for `page_match`-style strategies. Emitted verbatim inside `regex(...)`, so it is raw Ruby (e.g. `%r{v(\d+\.\d+)}i`).

skip.description: `true` forces the `skip "<reason>"` form even when `strategy`, `url` or `regex` is set. When unset or `false`, the livecheck is active when any of `strategy`, `url` or `regex` is set, and takes the skip form otherwise; `false` with none of the three set also logs a warning.

skip_reason.description: Reason text for the `skip "<reason>"` form. Default: `"Auto-generated on release."`.

strategy.description: `livecheck` strategy symbol (e.g. `github_latest`, `git`, `page_match`). Rendered as a Ruby symbol: `strategy :github_latest`.

url.description: `url` for the livecheck: a symbol naming one of the package's own URLs (`stable`, `head` or `homepage` in a formula; `url` or `homepage` in a cask), rendered `url :stable`, or a literal URL string rendered `url "https://..."`. A symbol the package does not have is an error. In an active livecheck that sets no url, a formula reads `:stable` and a cask reads `:url`.

HooksConfig.description:
A lifecycle hook block: `before:`, `after:`, `on_error:`, `always:`, or `before_publish:`. Each block carries a list of hook commands that run around the entire pipeline (not individual stages); which block a list sits under decides when it fires.

The key is `hooks:` in every block. The older `post:` spelling is still accepted, so `after: { post: [...] }` keeps working, with a deprecation warning. When a block sets a non-empty `hooks:` list and `post:`, the `hooks:` list runs and `post:` is ignored; an empty `hooks: []` beside a non-empty `post:` list runs the `post:` commands.

hooks.description: Commands to run when the block fires. The older `post:` key is read as this list.

post.description: Deprecated spelling of `hooks:` (anodizer before v0.4). Its commands run as the `hooks:` list, and it is ignored when `hooks:` is also set and non-empty.

HumanDuration.description: A duration: one or more whole numbers, each followed by a unit (ms, s, m, h or d), such as 90s, 1h30m or 2d. Spaces and tabs may separate the parts. The total may be at most one year (31536000s); a longer value is refused when the config loads.

IncludeFilePath.description: File path for a structured include.

path.description: Path to the include file (relative to the config file).

IncludeSpec.description:
An include specification: either a plain path string or a structured from_file/from_url.

YAML examples:

```yaml
includes:
  - ./defaults.yaml                           # plain string (backward compat)
  - from_file:
      path: ./config/release.yaml              # structured file path
  - from_url:
      url: https://example.com/config.yaml     # URL fetch
      headers:
        x-api-token: "${MYCOMPANY_TOKEN}"       # env var expansion in headers
```

anyOf.description: Structured URL include with `from_url.url` and optional headers.

IncludeUrlConfig.description: URL configuration for a structured include.

headers.description: Optional HTTP headers. Values support `${VAR_NAME}` environment variable expansion.

url.description: URL to fetch. If it does not start with `http://` or `https://`, `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/` is prepended (GitHub shorthand).

InstallScriptConfig.description:
`curl | sh` installer-script configuration.

Drives the install-script stage, which emits a deterministic POSIX `install.sh` as a release asset. At run time the script detects the host OS + architecture, maps it to the matching release archive, downloads and sha256-verifies it, extracts the binary, and installs it into an install directory (falling back to `$HOME/.local/bin` when the primary directory is not writable and no `sudo` is available).

Every field is optional: the repository slug is derived from the git `origin` remote, the installed binary names from the project name, the per-platform asset names from the release's configured targets (via the same engine SSOT that keeps cargo-binstall `pkg_url` from 404ing), and the checksums filename and tag prefix from the flagship crate that builds the project binary — so a bare `install_scripts: {}` produces a fully working installer with no required input.

base_url.description: Base URL the script downloads releases from and queries the REST API against (default: `https://github.com`). Point this at a GitHub Enterprise host to install from a self-hosted GitHub; the script derives the API base as `<base_url>/api/v3` for any non-`github.com` host.

binaries.description: Binary names to install out of the extracted archive (default: a single-element list of the project name). Every name is installed, so an archive shipping multiple binaries ships them all.

description.description: One-line description rendered into the script's header banner.

homepage.description: Project homepage URL rendered into the script's header banner.

id.description: Unique identifier for this install-script config (default: "default").

install_dir.description: Directory the binary is installed into (default: `/usr/local/bin`). The generated script falls back to `$HOME/.local/bin` when this directory is not writable and no `sudo` is available.

name.description: Human-readable name rendered into the script's header banner (default: the project name).

repo.description: GitHub `owner/name` slug the script downloads releases from (default: derived from the git `origin` remote).

skip.description: Skip this config. Accepts bool or template string. Accepts the legacy `disable:` spelling via serde alias for back-compat with imported configs.

verify_checksum.description: Whether the script verifies each download's sha256 checksum before installing (default: `true`). Set `false` only for repos that publish no checksums file or `.sha256` sidecars.

InstallSmokeConfig.description:
Per-package install smoke-test image overrides.

Each field is the container image used to install + version-check that package type. An unset field uses its default image (`debian:stable-slim`, `fedora:latest`, `alpine:latest`).

amd64_variant.description: amd64 microarchitecture variant filter (`v1` / `v2` / `v3` / `v4`). Only artifacts matching this variant are included. Default: `v1`. Typed as [`Amd64Variant`], so any value outside `v1`..`v4` is rejected when the config is parsed.

arm_variant.description: ARM version filter (e.g. "6", "7"). Only artifacts matching this variant are included. Default: `6`.

caveats.description: Post-install message shown to the user.

description.description: Full description of the kubectl plugin.

homepage.description: Project homepage URL for the plugin.

ids.description: Build IDs filter: only include artifacts whose `id` is in this list.

if.description: Template-conditional gate: when the rendered result is falsy (`"false"` / `"0"` / `"no"` / empty), the Krew publisher is skipped. Render failure hard-errors. Config key: `krews[].if:`. An absent, empty or blank `if:` imposes no gate and always runs; the falsy test applies to what a non-blank gate renders.

mode.description:
Which krew-index submission path to take.

- `auto` (default): probe whether the plugin already exists in `kubernetes-sigs/krew-index`. Already present → `bot` (the hosted krew-release-bot opens the version-bump PR server-side); definitively absent → `pr-direct` (anodizer opens the initial fork PR). A probe that can't reach a definitive answer (rate-limit, network error) hard-errors and does not guess, so a transient blip never routes an existing plugin into a maintainer-hostile fork PR.
- `bot`: always POST to the krew-release-bot webhook. Use when the plugin is known to be in krew-index and you want to skip the membership probe entirely.
- `pr-direct`: always open a fork PR against krew-index. Use for the initial submission, or a self-hosted krew-index mirror the hosted bot can't reach.

name.description: Override the plugin name (default: crate name).

repository.description: Unified repository config with branch, token, PR, git SSH support. (Replaces the legacy `manifests_repo:` / `upstream_repo:` form.) The upstream PR target is derived from `repository.pull_request.base` when set, falling back to the canonical kubernetes-sigs/krew-index.

required.description:
Override whether this publisher failing should fail the overall release.

Default: `false` — a failure here is logged but does not abort the release. Set to `true` to fail the release on any error.

retain_on_rollback.description: When `true`, a triggered rollback leaves this publisher's work in place and does not try to undo it. Default `false`.

short_description.description: One-line summary of the kubectl plugin (max 255 chars).

skip.description: Skip this Krew config. Accepts bool or template string (e.g. `"{{ if .IsSnapshot }}true{{ endif }}"` for conditional skip). Distinct from `skip_upload` so users can opt out of generating the manifest entirely (common when a project is not a kubectl plugin and has no krew channel).

skip_upload.description: Skip publishing. `"true"` always skips; `"auto"` skips for prereleases. Accepts bool or template string.

update_existing_pr.description: When true, force-push the updated plugin manifest to the existing PR branch when a PR for the same head branch already exists. The PR content is updated in place, so no duplicate is created. When false (default), the push is skipped and a warning is emitted so the operator sees that the publisher did not update the PR.

url_template.description: Custom URL template for download URLs (overrides release URL).

KrewMode.description:
Which krew-index submission path the krew publisher takes.

Selects between the self-contained krew-release-bot webhook and the fork-PR flow. Defaults to [`KrewMode::Auto`], which probes krew-index membership to decide.

oneOf.description: Probe krew-index membership and pick `bot` (present) or `pr-direct` (absent). An indeterminate probe hard-errors.
Always submit via the krew-release-bot webhook.

ManpagesConfig.description:
Man-page generation for an archive entry.

YAML examples:

```yaml
manpages:
  generate: "{{ ArtifactPath }} --man"     # mode A
  dst: "man/man1/"
# mode B: from_build_out: "**/out/{{ Binary }}.1"
# mode C: copy: "man/*.1"
```

from_build_out.description: Mode B: per-target glob harvesting man files a `build.rs` wrote into the crate's `OUT_DIR` (e.g. `"**/out/{{ Binary }}.1"`).

MCP server registry publisher configuration.

description.description: Clear human-readable description of server functionality (max 100 chars).

homepage.description: Optional URL to the server's homepage, documentation, or project website. Serialized as `websiteUrl` in the registry payload.

if.description: Template-conditional gate: when the rendered result is falsy (`"false"` / `"0"` / `"no"` / empty), the MCP publisher is skipped. Render failure hard-errors. The `mcp.if:` conditional gate. An absent, empty or blank `if:` imposes no gate and always runs; the falsy test applies to what a non-blank gate renders.

name.description: Server name in reverse-DNS format (e.g. `io.github.user/weather`). Must contain exactly one forward slash separating namespace from server name. An empty / unset value skips the publisher entirely.

packages.description: Distribution packages — one entry per package registry (npm, pypi, nuget, oci).

registry.description: Override the registry endpoint (for staging or a private mirror). Defaults to `https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io` when unset.

repository.description: Optional source repository metadata. Emitted as the `repository` object in the registry payload — omitted entirely when `url` is empty.

required.description:
Override whether this publisher failing should fail the overall release.

retain_on_rollback.description: When `true`, a triggered rollback leaves this publisher's work in place and does not try to undo it. Default `false`.

skip.description: Skip this publisher when the value is, or a Tera template renders, `true` or `1` (any letter case); `false`, `0` or empty runs it (e.g. `"{{ if .IsSnapshot }}true{{ endif }}"`). Accepts the legacy `disable:` spelling via serde alias for back-compat with imported configs (the MCP config field `MCP.Disable string`).

transport.description: Transport protocol configuration for this package.

MonorepoConfig.description:
Monorepo configuration.

When configured, tag discovery filters by `tag_prefix` and the working directory is scoped to `dir`.

The two `tag_prefix` keys work in opposite directions:
- `monorepo.tag_prefix`: tags in git already HAVE the prefix (e.g. `subproject1/v1.2.3`). The prefix is STRIPPED for `{{ Tag }}` while `{{ PrefixedTag }}` retains the full tag.
- `tag.tag_prefix`: a prefix to PREPEND when constructing `{{ PrefixedTag }}` from a plain tag.

When `monorepo` is configured, it takes precedence over `tag.tag_prefix` for `PrefixedTag` / `PrefixedPreviousTag` behavior.

dir.description:
Working directory for this subproject.

tag_prefix.description:
