owner.description: Repository owner (user or organization). Omitted or empty: inferred from the `origin` git remote, so a block may name only `token`.

token.description:
Auth token override for this repository, used in place of the default one. Useful when the release repository requires a different token than the one used to build from — for instance, when publishing to a repository in another organization. Supports templates (environment variables). Unset falls back to the pipeline token.

```yaml
release:
  github:
    owner: my-org
    name: my-repo
    token: "{{ .Env.RELEASE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}"
```

The token alone is enough when the release repository is the one `origin` points at:

```yaml
release:
  github:
    token: "{{ .Env.RELEASE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}"
```

amd64_variant.description: amd64 microarchitecture variant filter (`v1` / `v2` / `v3` / `v4`). Only artifacts matching this variant are included. Default: `v1`. Typed as [`Amd64Variant`], so any value outside `v1`..`v4` is rejected when the config is parsed.

checkver.description:
Scoop `checkver` strategy used by bucket maintainers to detect new releases. Defaults to `"github"` (derived from the configured GitHub repo) — `ScoopInstaller/Main` requires checkver for automated-update PRs. Override with a homepage regex when GitHub release detection is not appropriate.

Example: `checkver: "github"` or `checkver: "v([\\d.]+)"`.

description.description: Short description of the package (shown in `scoop info`).

directory.description: Subdirectory in the bucket repo for manifest placement. Defaults to `bucket` — scoop resolves manifests only from `bucket/` when that directory exists (root otherwise), so `bucket/` is correct for both layouts. Set to `""` to target the repo root. A stale same-named root-level manifest is removed when publishing into a subdirectory.

homepage.description: Project homepage URL. Falls back to the GitHub-derived URL when unset.

ids.description: Build IDs filter: only include artifacts whose `id` is in this list.

if.description: Template-conditional gate: when the rendered result is falsy (`"false"` / `"0"` / `"no"` / empty), the Scoop publisher is skipped. Render failure hard-errors. Config key: `scoop[].if:`. An absent, empty or blank `if:` imposes no gate and always runs; the falsy test applies to what a non-blank gate renders.

name.description: Override the manifest name (default: crate name).

persist.description: Data paths persisted between Scoop updates.

repository.description: The bucket repository: owner and name, plus branch, token, pull request and git SSH settings. Replaces the older `bucket:` key, which took only an owner and a name and is no longer accepted.

required.description:
Override whether this publisher failing should fail the overall release.

Default: `false` — a failure here is logged but does not abort the release. Set to `true` to fail the release on any error.

retain_on_rollback.description: When `true`, a triggered rollback leaves this publisher's work in place and does not try to undo it. Default `false`.

shortcuts.description: Start menu shortcuts as `[executable, label]` pairs.

skip_upload.description: Skip publishing the manifest.  `"true"` always skips; `"auto"` skips for prerelease versions. Accepts bool or template string.

url_template.description: Custom URL template for download URLs (overrides release URL).

args.description: Arguments passed to the signing command (supports templates with ${artifact} and ${signature}).

artifacts.description: Artifact types to sign: "none" (default), "all", "any", "archive", "binary", "checksum", "package", "installer", "diskimage", "macos_package", "snap", "source", "sbom" or "windows". `none` skips only this entry; a failing sibling entry still fails the stage.

asset_name_template.description:
`binary_signs:` only — override the release-asset name a binary signature uploads under.

Renders the asset's BASE name; the suffix the `signature:` / `certificate:` template appended to the binary's own file name still carries over, so one template names both assets (`app-1.0.0-linux-amd64` → `app-1.0.0-linux-amd64.sig` and `app-1.0.0-linux-amd64.pem`). Rendered in the same per-target scope an archive `name_template` renders under (`Os`, `Arch`, `Target`, the micro-architecture variants, `CrateName`, `Binary`).

```yaml
binary_signs:
  - artifacts: binary
    asset_name_template: "{{ Binary }}-{{ Version }}-{{ Target }}"
```

Unset, the name is derived from the crate's `archives:` config — see the signing docs.

authenticode.description: Authenticode (Windows PE/MSI) signing backend. When set, this sign config signs Windows artifacts in place via osslsigncode (Linux/cross) or signtool (Windows), and no detached cosign/gpg signature is written. The signing command, argv, timestamp URL, and artifact selector are all derived; supply only the cert (a secret).

certificate.description: Certificate file to embed in the signature (Cosign bundle signing).

env.description: Environment variables passed to the signing command.

id.description: Unique identifier for this sign config.

ids.description: Build IDs filter: only sign artifacts from builds whose `id` is in this list.

if.description: Template-conditional: skip this sign config when the gate renders `false`, `0`, `no` or empty (any letter case). An absent, empty or blank `if:` imposes no gate and always runs; the falsy test applies to what a non-blank gate renders.

output.description: Capture and log stdout/stderr of the signing command. Accepts bool or template string (e.g., "{{ IsSnapshot }}").

stdin.description: Content written to the signing command's stdin (e.g. a passphrase), rendered as a template (`{{ Env.GPG_PASSPHRASE }}`). The rendered value is a credential: leading and trailing whitespace is removed, and a template that does not render is an error naming `signs[<id or index>].stdin` without the template's text.

stdin_file.description: Path to a file whose content is written to the signing command's stdin.

verify.description: Post-sign verification knobs. Verification is ON by default wherever its inputs are derivable (keyed cosign, keyless cosign on GitHub Actions, gpg); set `verify: { enabled: false }` to disable, or supply the keyless certificate identity / issuer when they cannot be derived from the environment.

SignVerifyConfig.description:
Post-sign verification settings shared by [`SignConfig`] and [`DockerSignConfig`].

After each signature is produced, the sign stage re-verifies it with the matching verifier (`cosign verify-blob` for detached cosign signatures, `cosign verify` for registry-attached docker signatures, `gpg --verify` for gpg) so "the signer exited 0" is upgraded to "the signature actually verifies". Everything is derived when possible:

- **keyed cosign** — the public key is derived once per run via `cosign public-key --key <ref>`; nothing to configure.
- **keyless cosign** — the certificate identity/issuer are derived from the ambient GitHub Actions OIDC environment (`GITHUB_SERVER_URL`/`GITHUB_WORKFLOW_REF`); outside GitHub Actions, supply them here or verification skips with a named reason.
- **gpg** — verified against the same keyring that signed.

```yaml
signs:
  - cmd: cosign
    args: ["sign-blob", "--bundle={{ Signature }}", "--yes", "{{ Artifact }}"]
    verify:
      certificate_identity: "https://github.com/acme/app/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/tags/v1.0.0"
      certificate_oidc_issuer: "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
```

certificate_identity.description: Exact certificate identity (SAN) expected in a keyless signing certificate (`cosign --certificate-identity`). Overrides the value derived from the GitHub Actions environment.

certificate_identity_regexp.description: Regular expression matched against the keyless certificate identity (`cosign --certificate-identity-regexp`). Ignored when [`certificate_identity`](Self::certificate_identity) is set.

certificate_oidc_issuer.description: Expected OIDC issuer of the keyless signing certificate (`cosign --certificate-oidc-issuer`). Overrides the derived GitHub Actions issuer.

enabled.description: Whether to verify each produced signature (default: `true`).

attachments.description: Slack legacy attachments (typed for schema validation).

blocks.description: Slack Block Kit blocks (typed for schema validation).

enabled.description: Enable Slack announcements (supports template expressions).

icon_emoji.description: Override the webhook's default icon with an emoji (e.g. ":rocket:").

icon_url.description: Override the webhook's default icon with an image URL.

message_template.description: Message template for the Slack post. Default: "{{ ProjectName }} {{ Tag }} is out! Check it out at {{ ReleaseURL }}"

username.description: Username the message is posted as (e.g. "release-bot"). Default: `anodizer`.

webhook_url.description: Slack incoming webhook URL. Use template `{{ Env.SLACK_WEBHOOK }}` to reference an environment variable.

SlackAttachment.description: A Slack legacy attachment. Common fields are typed; additional fields are captured via flatten.

color.description: Attachment sidebar color (hex string, e.g., "#36a64f" for green).

fallback.description: Plain-text summary shown in notifications that cannot render attachments.

footer.description: Small text shown at the bottom of the attachment.

pretext.description: Text shown above the attachment block.

text.description: Main body text of the attachment (supports template variables).

title.description: Bold title text at the top of the attachment.

SlackBlock.description: A Slack Block Kit block element. Common fields are typed; additional block-type-specific fields are captured via flatten.

text.description: Text object for the block (used by header, section, context types).

emoji.description: Whether to render emoji shortcodes (plain_text only).

SmokeImage.description: A single per-package smoke-test image selection.

after.description: Services that must start before this app.

args.description: Additional arguments passed to the command.

before.description: Services that must start after this app.

command.description: Command to run (relative to snap root).

command_chain.description: Wrapper commands run before the main command.

completer.description: Path to bash completion script relative to snap.

daemon.description: Daemon type: simple, forking, oneshot, notify, dbus.

desktop.description: Path to .desktop file relative to snap.

environment.description: Environment variables for the app (supports string, integer, and boolean values).

passthrough.description: Arbitrary YAML passed through to snap.yaml.

post_stop_command.description: Command to run after daemon stops.

restart_condition.description: Restart condition: on-failure, always, on-success, on-abnormal, on-abort, on-watchdog, never.

stop_command.description: Command to gracefully stop the daemon.

stop_mode.description: How to stop the daemon: sigterm, sigkill, etc.

apps.description: Application configurations defining daemons, commands, env vars.

base.description: Runtime base snap: core, core18, core20, core22, core24, bare.

channel_templates.description: Distribution channels: edge, beta, candidate, stable.

confinement.description: Security confinement level: strict, devmode, classic.

description.description: Extended description (user-facing in store).

extra_files.description: Additional static files to bundle (string shorthand or structured form).

hooks.description: Snap hooks — maps hook name to arbitrary hook config.

icon.description:
Path to the snap icon image (`.png` or `.svg`).

When set, anodizer copies the file to `meta/gui/<name>.<ext>` inside the staged prime directory before `snapcraft pack` runs. The icon is delivered to the Snap Store via snapcraft's GUI metadata channel and never appears in `snap.json`, keeping uploads schema-clean. (The Snap Store rejects `snap.json` that contains an `icon:` key with "Additional properties are not allowed ('icon' was unexpected)".)

The source path may be absolute or relative to the project root. Anodizer errors before staging if the file does not exist.

id.description: Unique identifier for this snapcraft config.

ids.description: Build IDs to include. Empty means all builds.

if.description: Template-conditional gate: when the rendered result is falsy (`"false"` / `"0"` / `"no"` / empty), the snapcraft config is skipped. Render failure hard-errors. The `snapcrafts[].if:`. Distinct from `skip:` (always-skip predicate). An absent, empty or blank `if:` imposes no gate and always runs; the falsy test applies to what a non-blank gate renders.

layout.description:
Directory mappings for sandbox accessibility.

Accepts the legacy plural `layouts:` spelling via serde alias for back-compat with imported configs.

name.description: Snap package name in the store.

name_template.description: Template for the output snap filename.

plugs.description: Top-level snap plug definitions (structured map). Keys are plug names, values are either `null` (simple plug) or an object with `interface` and optional attributes (e.g. `{ interface: "content", target: "$SNAP/shared" }`). An arbitrary key/value map for this field.

publish.description: Whether to publish to the snapcraft store.

replace.description: Remove source archives from artifacts, keeping only snap.

required.description:
When `true`, a failed snap upload counts as a required-publisher failure: trips the submitter gate and appears in `report.required_failures()` so the CLI exits non-zero.

Default: `false` — a failed snap upload does not abort the pipeline. It is still reported as a post-publish delivery issue by `verify-release` regardless of this setting: `required` governs only whether the run ABORTS mid-pipeline. It has no say in whether an attempted failure gets certified as a clean release.

When multiple snapcraft configs exist, the stage records ONE aggregated `PublisherResult`: `required = true` if ANY config opted in.

skip.description: Skip this snapcraft config. Accepts bool or template string (e.g. `"{{ if .IsSnapshot }}true{{ endif }}"` for conditional skip). Accepts the legacy `disable:` spelling via serde alias for back-compat.

templated_extra_files.description: Extra files whose contents are rendered through the template engine before bundling. Unlike `extra_files` which copy as-is, template variables like `{{ Tag }}` are expanded.

SnapcraftExtraFileSpec.description: Specifies an extra file for snapcraft. Can be a simple source path string or a structured object with source, destination, and mode fields (matching the snapcraft extra-files shape).

anyOf.description: Structured form with source, destination, and mode.

bind.description: Bind-mount a directory to the snap's layout.

bind_file.description: Bind-mount a single file to the snap's layout.

symlink.description: Symlink a path to a location in the snap.

version_template.description: Version string template for snapshot builds (e.g., "{{ Commit }}-SNAPSHOT"). Accepts the deprecated `name_template:` alias (renamed to `version_template`): a non-empty `name_template` is folded into `version_template`. A deprecation warning is emitted at config-load time when the alias is hit (see `apply_snapshot_legacy_aliases`).

enabled.description: When true, generate a source code archive for the release.

files.description: Extra files to include in the source archive. Accepts strings (glob patterns) or objects with `src`, `dst`, `info` and `strip_parent` keys.

format.description: Archive format for the source tarball: tar.gz, tgz, tar, or zip (default: tar.gz).

name_template.description: Filename template for the source archive (supports templates).

prefix_template.description: Prefix prepended to all paths inside the archive (supports templates). Defaults to name_template value. Use this to set a different prefix than the archive name.

SourceFileEntry.description: An individual file entry for the source archive, with `src`, `dst`, `strip_parent` and `info` (file metadata overrides) keys.

dst.description: Destination path within the archive prefix directory.

src.description: Source file path or glob pattern.

strip_parent.description: Strip the parent directory from the source path.

SourceFileInfo.description: File metadata overrides for source archive entries.

mode.description: File permissions mode. Accepts a YAML int (decimal) or an octal-prefixed string (`"0o755"`, `"0755"`). Stored as a `u32` after parsing — see [`StringOrU32`].

mtime.description: Modification time in RFC3339 format (supports templates).

bins.description: Map of binary name → install path declared in the spec's `%files` section. Each entry tells the generated `.spec` which installed file the package owns. When omitted, each binary produced by the build for this crate defaults to `%{_bindir}/<name>` (i.e. `/usr/bin/<name>`, the RPM-idiomatic location for a built binary). Provide this only to override the install path or to declare extra owned paths. The `%files` section lists the entries in alphabetical order of binary name.

build_host.description: Override the build host recorded in the RPM header. Useful for reproducible builds where the actual hostname leaks build-env detail.

contents.description: Additional contents to include in the source RPM. Takes the same entries as `crates[].nfpms[].contents`; the SRPM-style `source:` / `destination:` / `type:` keys are accepted as aliases.

description.description: Package description.

enabled.description: Enable source RPM generation. Default: false.

posttrans.description: `%posttrans` scriptlet — executed *after* all packages in the transaction have been installed. Path to a script file.

prefixes.description: Filesystem prefixes the package may install to (RPM `Prefix:` tag). Each entry becomes one `Prefix:` directive — relocatable RPMs need at least one prefix declared.

prerelease.description: Prerelease suffix appended to the version (e.g. `rc1`, `beta2`).

pretrans.description: `%pretrans` scriptlet — executed on the package transaction *before* any package in the transaction is installed. Path to a script file.

signature.description: RPM signature configuration. Takes the same keys as `crates[].nfpms[].rpm.signature`.

skip.description: Skip this config. Accepts bool or template string.

spec_file.description: Path to the RPM spec file template.

version_metadata.description: Build metadata appended to the version (e.g. git commit hash).

StringOrBool.description: A value that can be either a bool or a template string. Used by `skip`, `skip_upload`, and similar fields across multiple config structs to support both `skip: true` and template conditionals like `skip: "{{ if .IsSnapshot }}true{{ endif }}"`. An unquoted `1` or `0` loads as `true` or `false`.

StringOrU32.description:
A value that can be either a `u32` or a string parsed as octal/decimal.

Used by `NfpmConfig.umask` (and any future field specified as `int OR string` in YAML — the parser canonicalizes both forms to a `u32`). Accepts: `0o022`, `"0o022"`, `"022"`, `"18"`, `18`. Bare numeric YAML values are interpreted as decimal; YAML-string forms accept the `0o`/`0O` prefix to spell octal explicitly.

artifacts.description: Artifact-kind filter (`before_publish:` only). When set, the hook fires only for artifacts whose kind matches the filter. Unset is the same as `all` (every artifact). Ignored by lifecycle hook sites for the same reason as `ids`.

cmd.description:
Command to run.

The entire string is interpreted by `sh -c`, so shell metacharacters (`|`, `;`, `&&`, backticks, `$()`, redirects, globs) are honoured — any templated values folded into `cmd` become part of the shell command and are subject to word-splitting and metacharacter expansion. Keep templated user-config values out of `cmd` when possible, or quote them defensively (e.g. `'{{ Env.FOO }}'`). Hooks already run with `env_clear()` plus an allow-list, so secrets in `$ENV` are not inherited unless explicitly listed in `env`.

dir.description: Working directory for the command (defaults to project root).

ids.description: Artifact-id allow-list (`before_publish:` only). When set, the hook fires only for artifacts whose id matches one of these strings. Unset (the default) imposes no id constraint. Ignored by lifecycle hook sites (`before:` / `after:` / per-build / per-archive) — those run once per pipeline tick and never per artifact.

if.description: Template-conditional: when set, the hook only runs if the rendered result is truthy (not `"false"` / `"0"` / `"no"` / empty). Render failure hard-errors and is never skipped silently. An absent, empty or blank `if:` imposes no gate and always runs; the falsy test applies to what a non-blank gate renders. The gate is evaluated before the hook's own `env:` is rendered, so it cannot read those entries: a skipped hook's env is never rendered and cannot fail.

output.description: When true, capture and log stdout/stderr of the command.

run_once.description: Run the hook exactly once before the publish stage, with no per-artifact runs (`before_publish:` only). With the default `false`, the hook keeps the per-artifact semantics: it fires once for each artifact passing the `ids` / `artifacts` filters, with the per-artifact template vars (`ArtifactName`, `ArtifactPath`, ...) and the `$ANODIZER_ARTIFACT` channel bound. With `true`, the hook runs a single time with the run-level template vars (`Version`, `Tag`, ...); the `ids` / `artifacts` filters and the per-artifact vars do not apply, so the command is expected to iterate the dist directory itself.

branch_history.description: Branch history mode for determining the previous tag: "full" or "last".

bump_minor_pre_major.description: While the current major version is `0`, demote a conventional breaking change (`feat!:` / `BREAKING CHANGE`) from a major bump to a minor bump (e.g. `0.5.0` → `0.6.0`, where the bump would otherwise give `1.0.0`). Honors the SemVer rule that anything may change in the `0.y.z` range. An explicit `#major`/`#minor` token, a `custom_tag`, or a manually-ahead `Cargo.toml` version always wins over this demotion. No-op once a real tag reaches `1.x`. Default false.

bump_patch_for_minor_pre_major.description: While the current major version is `0`, demote a conventional feature (`feat:`) from a minor bump to a patch bump (e.g. `0.5.0` → `0.5.1`, where the bump would otherwise give `0.6.0`). Independent of `bump_minor_pre_major`. An explicit token / `custom_tag` / ahead `Cargo.toml` always wins. No-op at `1.x`. Default false.

custom_tag.description: Custom version tag. When set, no auto-increment happens.

default_bump.description: Default bump when a commit range carries no explicit `#` token and no conventional-commit marker: "major", "minor", "patch", or "none". Defaults to "none" — a range of only chore/docs/style/refactor/test/ build/ci commits produces no release (the conventional-commit contract). Set "patch"/"minor" to cut a release on every range regardless of type.

force_without_changes.description: When true, create a new tag even if no commits have changed since the last tag.

force_without_changes_pre.description: Like force_without_changes but only for pre-release versions.

git_api_tagging.description:
When true, use the GitHub/GitLab API for tagging. When false, the git CLI creates the tag.

Mutually exclusive with `sign` on a pushed tag: the API creates the tag object server-side and cannot apply your local GPG/SSH signature, so anodizer errors and ships no silently-unsigned tag. Use local tagging (drop `git_api_tagging`) to create signed tags.

initial_version.description: Version string to use when no previous tag exists (default: "0.1.0").

major_string_token.description: Conventional commit token triggering a major bump (default: "major").

minor_string_token.description: Conventional commit token triggering a minor bump (default: "minor" or "feat").

none_string_token.description: Conventional commit token suppressing a version bump entirely (default: "none").

patch_string_token.description: Conventional commit token triggering a patch bump (default: "patch" or "fix").

prerelease.description: When true, apply a pre-release suffix to the generated version.

push.description: When true, `anodizer tag` also pushes the version-sync bump commit to the release branch (atomically with the tag) as well as the tag. CLI `--push` / `--no-push` override this. Default false preserves the "push the tag, inspect the branch locally before pushing" workflow.

release_branches.description: Branch name patterns (supports wildcards) that trigger releases (default: ["master", "main"]).

sign.description:
When true, anodizer creates the version tag with `git tag -s` (a cryptographically signed annotated tag). The default is `git tag -a` (unsigned annotated tag). The signing key and method are taken entirely from the user's git configuration (`user.signingkey`, and `gpg.format` to select GPG vs SSH signing) — anodizer adds no key field of its own, so both GPG and SSH signing work with no anodizer-specific setup. Applies in every workspace mode: single-crate, lockstep, and per-crate — every tag anodizer cuts is signed when this is enabled. The CLI `--sign` / `--no-sign` flags override this per invocation. Default (unset or false) leaves the existing unsigned annotated-tag behavior unchanged.

Mutually exclusive with `git_api_tagging` on a pushed tag: the GitHub API creates the tag object on the remote and cannot apply a local signature, so combining the two on a push is a hard error. Signing works with local tagging and with `--push-tags-only` (both cut the tag locally first).

skip_ci_on_bump.description:
Append `[skip ci]` to the version-sync bump commit subject.

Off by default. Only enable with a `workflow_run`-triggered release workflow: `[skip ci]` on the bump commit (which becomes the tag target) ALSO suppresses an `on: push: tags:` release trigger, so enabling this with a tag-push-triggered release silently skips the release. Leave off for the tag-push pattern; enable for the `workflow_run` pattern to skip the (already crate-gated, harmless) redundant CI re-run.

tag_context.description: Source for determining the previous tag: "repo" (default) or "branch".

tag_post_hooks.description: Commands to run after `anodizer tag` successfully creates the tag (and, when a push was requested, pushes it). Env and template vars same as `tag_pre_hooks`.

tag_pre_hooks.description: Commands to run before `anodizer tag` creates the tag. Useful for updating lockfiles or committing sibling changes that must be part of the tagged commit. Env: `ANODIZER_CURRENT_TAG`, `ANODIZER_PREVIOUS_TAG` are set; template vars `{{ Tag }}`, `{{ PreviousTag }}`, `{{ Version }}`, `{{ PrefixedTag }}` are available.

tag_prefix.description:
Prefix prepended to version tags (e.g., "v" produces "v1.2.3").

Also names the tag family every crate that omits `tag_template` releases under: a crate with no template of its own and no `defaults.crates.tag_template` derives `<tag_prefix>{{ Version }}` at config load, so `tag`, `release`, `bump` and `changelog` all agree on the same tag.

```yaml
tag:
  tag_prefix: "rel-"
crates:
  - { name: core, path: crates/core }   # tag family rel-{{ Version }}
  - { name: cli, path: crates/cli }     # tag family rel-{{ Version }}
```

verbose.description: When true, print verbose tag calculation output.

color.description: Theme color for the card (hex string, e.g. "0076D7").

enabled.description: Enable Microsoft Teams announcements (supports template expressions).

icon_url.description: Icon URL displayed in the card header.

message_template.description: Message template for the Adaptive Card body. Default: "{{ ProjectName }} {{ Tag }} is out! Check it out at {{ ReleaseURL }}"

title_template.description: Title template for the Adaptive Card header. Default: "{{ ProjectName }} {{ Tag }} is out!"

bot_token.description:
Telegram Bot API token. Get one from @BotFather.

Prefer `{{ Env.TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN }}` over an in-config literal — plaintext tokens grant full bot impersonation and are NOT redacted from error messages or `dist/config.yaml` after a dry-run / snapshot run.

chat_id.description: Telegram chat ID to send the message to (supports template variables).

enabled.description: Enable Telegram announcements. Requires bot_token and chat_id (supports template expressions).

message_template.description: Message template. Default: "{{ ProjectName | mdv2escape }} {{ Tag | mdv2escape }} is out\\! Check it out at {{ ReleaseURL | mdv2escape }}"

message_thread_id.description: Message thread ID for sending to a specific topic in a forum group. Supports template expressions; parsed to i64 at runtime.

TemplateFileConfig.description:
Configuration for a template file that is rendered through the template engine and placed in the dist directory as a release artifact.

All rendered template files are uploaded to the release by default. Both `src` and `dst` paths support template rendering.

dst.description: Destination filename, prefixed with the dist directory. Templates: allowed.

id.description: Identifier for this template file entry (default: "default").

mode.description: File permissions in octal notation as a string, e.g. `"0755"` (default: `"0655"`). Quote it so YAML does not read it as a decimal number.

skip.description: Skip this entry when the value is, or a Tera template renders, `true` or `1` (any letter case); `false`, `0` or empty keeps it (e.g. `'{{ if eq .Os "windows" }}true{{ end }}'`). Works like `skip:` in `changelog:`, `checksum:` and the publishers.

src.description: Source template file path. The file contents are rendered through the template engine. Templates: allowed (in path itself).

TemplatedExtraFile.description: A file whose contents are rendered through the template engine before use. Used by `templated_extra_files` across multiple stages.

dst.description: Destination filename for the rendered output. Supports template variables (e.g. `"{{ ProjectName }}-NOTES.txt"`).

mode.description: File permissions in octal notation as a string, e.g. `"0755"`. Parsed at runtime via `parse_octal_mode()` to avoid YAML interpreting as decimal.

enabled.description: Enable Twitter/X announcements. Requires TWITTER_CONSUMER_KEY, TWITTER_CONSUMER_SECRET, TWITTER_ACCESS_TOKEN, TWITTER_ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET env vars (supports template expressions).

message_template.description: Tweet message template. Default: "{{ ProjectName }} {{ Tag }} is out! Check it out at {{ ReleaseURL }}"

hooks.description: Pre/post hooks around universal binary creation.

id.description: Unique identifier for this universal binary, propagated into the artifact's metadata as `id`.

ids.description:
Build IDs filter: only combine binaries from builds whose `id` is in this list. A build's `id` defaults to its binary name.

When unset, the filter is this entry's `id` if set; otherwise the project name when a binary of the crate carries that id; otherwise the crate name.

mod_timestamp.description: Override the modification timestamp for reproducible universal binaries.

name_template.description: Output filename template for the universal binary (supports templates).

replace.description: When true, remove the individual arch binaries after creating the universal binary.

checksum_header.description: Header name for the SHA256 checksum of the artifact.

client_x509_cert.description: Path to PEM-encoded client X.509 certificate for mTLS.

client_x509_key.description: Path to PEM-encoded client X.509 key for mTLS.

custom_artifact_name.description: When true, use the artifact name as-is (don't append to target URL).

custom_headers.description: Custom HTTP headers (each value is template-expanded).

exclude.description:
Glob patterns matched against each artifact's file name; anodizer drops any artifact whose name matches at least one glob from THIS upload target only. Use it to keep heavy sidecars (checksums, signatures, SBOMs) off a given endpoint while archives still upload. Composes with `ids:` and `exts:` (all filters apply). Unset or empty keeps everything.

```yaml
uploads:
  - name: mirror
    target: "https://mirror.example.com/{{ .ArtifactName }}"
    exclude: ["*.sha256", "*.sig", "*.cdx.json"]
```

extra_files.description: Extra files to include in uploading.

extra_files_only.description: Upload only extra files, skip normal artifacts.

exts.description: File extension filter: only upload artifacts with these extensions.

ids.description: Build IDs filter: only upload artifacts whose `id` is in this list.

if.description: Template-conditional gate: when the rendered result is falsy (`"false"` / `"0"` / `"no"` / empty), the upload is skipped. Render failure hard-errors. The `uploads[].if:` conditional gate. An absent, empty or blank `if:` imposes no gate and always runs; the falsy test applies to what a non-blank gate renders.

meta.description: Include `dist/metadata.json` in uploaded artifacts. The sibling `dist/artifacts.json` manifest is never uploaded.

method.description: HTTP method: PUT or POST (default: PUT).

name.description: Name of this upload entry. Required: an entry without one is skipped. It keys the credential env vars `UPLOAD_{NAME}_USERNAME` and `UPLOAD_{NAME}_SECRET`, uppercased with each `-` turned into `_`.

overwrite.description:
Re-upload an artifact even when an identical one already exists at the target path (default: `false`).

With the default, a re-run that finds the same version's artifact already uploaded with a matching SHA-256 records an idempotent SKIP and does not PUT it again, so re-running a partially-failed release is safe. A path that already holds a *different* artifact for the same version still hard-errors (immutable-version drift) unless `overwrite` is set. With `overwrite: true`, every artifact is PUT unconditionally.

password.description:
Password for HTTP basic auth.

Strongly prefer `{{ Env.UPLOAD_PASSWORD }}` (or any other env-var template) over an in-config literal — plaintext values here are NOT redacted from dry-run output and will end up in `dist/config.yaml` when the pipeline runs with `--dry-run` / `--snapshot`. Resolution order: rendered `password` template → env `UPLOAD_{NAME}_SECRET`.

required.description:
Override whether this upload failing should fail the overall release.

Default: `false` — a failure here is logged but does not abort the release. Set to `true` to fail the release on any error.

retain_on_rollback.description: When `true`, a triggered rollback leaves this upload's artifacts in place and sends no server-side DELETE. Default `false`.

skip.description: Skip this upload when the value is, or a template renders, `true` or `1` (any letter case).

target.description: Target URL template (supports template variables like {{ ProjectName }}, {{ Version }}).

trusted_certificates.description: Path to PEM-encoded trusted CA certificates.

username.description: Username for HTTP basic auth. Resolution order: rendered `username` template → env `UPLOAD_{NAME}_USERNAME`. Set this to a literal value or a `{{ Env.X }}` template.

brute.description: Use brute-force compression (--brute flag). Very slow but produces smallest output.

compress.description: UPX compression level string (e.g., "1"-"9", "best"). Maps to `--compress` flag.

enabled.description: Whether to compress binaries with UPX. Accepts a bool or a template string that evaluates to a bool.

id.description: Unique identifier for this UPX config.

ids.description: Build IDs filter: only compress binaries from builds whose `id` is in this list.

required.description: When true, fail the build if UPX is not found.

targets.description: Target triples to compress binaries for (empty means all targets).

VerifyReleaseConfig.description:
Top-level `verify_release:` block.

See the module-level docs for the verification lifecycle. The gate is a no-op unless `enabled: true`.

assert_assets.description: Assert that every produced artifact has a matching uploaded asset on the published release, and that every signature / certificate / SBOM asset the resolved `signs:` / `sboms:` config demands exists there too (derived from config + the artifact set, so a sign or SBOM stage that silently produced nothing still fails the gate with the exact missing names; intentional skips — `if:` falsy, `skip:` truthy, `--skip=sign` — create no expectations). Default `true` (no extra config: anodizer already knows the produced set and can fetch the release's asset list). Independent of Docker and the network smoke-test.

assert_landing.description: Assert that every publisher that succeeded this run is actually VISIBLE upstream: each published crate version is visible on the crates.io sparse index, each npm package version is visible on its registry, each uploaded PyPI wheel or source distribution is listed by the index it went to, each uploaded blob object exists in its bucket, each uploaded snap is live in the Snap Store's channel map (catching a manual-review hold that parked the revision outside every channel), and each docker image tag the run pushed answers a registry manifest `GET` at the digest the push recorded. Default `true` (no extra config: the run's own publish report and artifact set already carry every coordinate the probes need). Publishers that did not run — or did not succeed — are skipped, as is an image the run built without pushing. A target the registry has not served yet is re-asked (5s backoff doubling to a 30s cap) inside ONE 12-minute window shared by the whole sweep, shortened whenever `retry.max_elapsed` leaves less than that; an absence is reported when the window closes.

enabled.description: Whether to run the post-release verification gate at all. Default `false` — the gate is opt-in because it needs the published release to already exist (it runs after publish) and, for install-smoke, a Docker daemon.

glibc_ceiling.description: glibc version ceiling, e.g. `"2.36"`. When any glibc-linked `.deb` requires a glibc NEWER than this floor, the gate reports it and exits non-zero. Unset (the default) disables the libc check entirely. musl binaries have no glibc requirement and are skipped.

install_smoke.description: Per-package install smoke-test images. When unset, smoke-testing is off. When present, each package type that produced an artifact is installed in its (configured or default) container and `<bin> --version` is run.

VersionFileEntry.description:
One `version_files` enrollment.

Accepts two forms:
- **Bare path** — every occurrence of the version in the file is rewritten.

  ```yaml
  version_files:
    - docs/installation.md
  ```

- **Anchored** — a path plus a `match` regex that selects this enrollment's own occurrences, so two crates can share one file (and even one literal) without rewriting each other's lines.

  ```yaml
  version_files:
    - path: chart/cfgd/values.yaml
      match: 'operator:\s+image:.*:v{version}'
  ```

anyOf.description: Bare repo-root-relative path — a whole-file sweep.
Path plus a regex anchor scoping the rewrite to its own occurrences.

enabled.description: When true, synchronize the crate version with the git tag during release.

mode.description: Sync mode: "cargo" (updates Cargo.toml) or "tag" (derives version from tag).

WaitForWorkspaceDepsConfig.description:
Pre-publish polling gate for `cargo publish`. When `enabled`, the cargo publisher reads its crate's manifest, identifies every dep that points at another crate in the same anodizer workspace, and polls `https://index.crates.io/<prefix>/<name>` until each `(name, version)` pair is queryable. Only then does `cargo publish` run.

Default: disabled. Anodizer's own workspaces publish lockstep with one tag; this feature only kicks in for multi-tag-multi-crate workspaces like cfgd where downstream crates can otherwise race the sparse-index propagation of their upstream deps.

Complementary to `cargo.index_timeout`: this gate runs BEFORE publish (waits for *upstream* deps to arrive), while `index_timeout` runs AFTER publish (waits for the *just-published* crate to arrive before the next dependent in the same run starts).

```yaml
crates:
  - name: myapp
    path: .
    publish:
      cargo:
        wait_for_workspace_deps:
          enabled: true
          poll_interval: 5s
          max_wait: 5m
```

enabled.description: Master switch. Default `false` preserves today's behavior for single-crate workspaces and lockstep monorepos.

max_wait.description: Hard ceiling on the total wait. The publisher bails with a clear error once `max_wait` elapses without every dep appearing. Humantime-style string (e.g. `"5m"`, `"30s"`). Default: `"5m"`.

poll_interval.description: Time between successive index probes. Humantime-style string (e.g. `"5s"`, `"500ms"`, `"1m"`). Default: `"5s"`.

enabled.description: Enable generic webhook announcements (supports template expressions).

endpoint_url.description:
Webhook endpoint URL (supports template variables).

Prefer `{{ Env.WEBHOOK_URL }}` for any URL containing a secret token in its path / query string — plaintext values are NOT redacted from error messages or `dist/config.yaml` after a dry-run / snapshot run.

expected_status_codes.description: HTTP status codes to accept as success (default: [200, 201, 202, 204]).

headers.description:
Custom HTTP headers to include in the request.

Precedence — **anodizer-specific**:
- anodizer: a config-supplied `Authorization` header wins over the `BASIC_AUTH_HEADER_VALUE` / `BEARER_TOKEN_HEADER_VALUE` env var.
- The conventional behaviour: env-supplied `Authorization` is appended FIRST; most servers honour the first occurrence, so the env value effectively wins.

Migrating configs that relied on env-overriding the config header must either remove the config entry or be reconfigured. Use templated config (`Authorization: "Bearer {{ Env.MY_TOKEN }}"`) for the cleanest migration.

message_template.description: Message body template. Default: "{{ ProjectName }} {{ Tag }} is out! Check it out at {{ ReleaseURL }}"

skip_tls_verify.description: When true, skip TLS certificate verification for the webhook endpoint.

additional_locales.description:
Locale manifests published beside the default locale manifest, one `<PackageIdentifier>.locale.<locale>.yaml` per entry. Each entry names its `locale` and may override any localizable field; a field left unset takes the default locale's value, so a translation only has to carry the text that differs. Every field supports templates, and `release_notes` reads `Changelog` the way the top-level field does.

An entry whose `locale` renders empty, equals `default_locale`, or repeats an earlier entry's locale skips the crate before any manifest is written or pushed.

```yaml
winget:
  default_locale: "en-US"
  additional_locales:
    - locale: "pt-BR"
      short_description: "Gerencia widgets"
      description: "Uma ferramenta completa para gerenciar widgets."
    - locale: "de-DE"
      short_description: "Verwaltet Widgets"
```

amd64_variant.description: amd64 microarchitecture variant filter (`v1` / `v2` / `v3` / `v4`). Only artifacts matching this variant are included. Default: `v1`. Typed as [`Amd64Variant`], so any value outside `v1`..`v4` is rejected when the config is parsed.

default_locale.description:
Locale stamped into the WinGet manifests: the version manifest's `DefaultLocale`, the installer manifest's `InstallerLocale`, the locale manifest's `PackageLocale`, and the locale manifest's `.locale.<locale>.yaml` file name. Supports templates. Default: `en-US`.

```yaml
winget:
  default_locale: "pt-BR"
```

description.description: Full package description displayed in the WinGet gallery.

documentations.description:
Documentation links rendered as the `Documentations[]` block on the locale manifest. Each entry is a `{ label, url }` pair shown in the winget gallery (real ripgrep emits a `FAQ` and a `User Guide` entry). Omitted entirely when empty.

Example:

```yaml
documentations:
  - label: "User Guide"
    url: "https://github.com/owner/repo/blob/master/GUIDE.md"
```

ids.description: Build IDs filter: only include artifacts whose `id` is in this list.

if.description: Template-conditional gate: when the rendered result is falsy (`"false"` / `"0"` / `"no"` / empty), the WinGet publisher is skipped. Render failure hard-errors. Config key: `winget[].if:`. An absent, empty or blank `if:` imposes no gate and always runs; the falsy test applies to what a non-blank gate renders.

installation_notes.description: Post-install notes shown to the user.

moniker.description:
Short invoke alias shown as the package `Moniker` (e.g. `rg` for ripgrep, `fd` for fd). This is the command users type, NOT the package/crate name. When unset, anodizer derives it from the single published binary name; with multiple binaries and no override the Moniker is omitted (winget treats it as optional).

Example: `moniker: "rg"`.

name.description: Override the package name (default: crate name).

package_identifier.description: WinGet package identifier (e.g. "Publisher.AppName"), template-rendered. Auto-generated as `<publisher>.<name>` if empty.

package_name.description: Package name as displayed (default: same as name).

path.description: Manifest file path (auto-generated if empty from publisher/name/version).

post_publish_poll.description: Post-publish PR-validation polling settings. Polling is disabled by default — winget-pkgs PR validation routinely takes hours to days, and blocking a CI workflow on that wait is wrong. Opt in per-publisher with `post_publish_poll: { enabled: true }` when running locally and willing to wait, or disable globally via `--no-post-publish-poll`.

product_code.description: Product code for the installer (used in Add/Remove Programs).

publisher_url.description: Publisher homepage URL shown in the WinGet manifest.

repository.description: The manifests repository: owner and name, plus branch, token, pull request and git SSH settings. Replaces the older `manifests_repo:` key, which is no longer accepted.

required.description:
Override whether this publisher failing should fail the overall release.

Default: `false` — a failure here is logged but does not abort the release. Set to `true` to fail the release on any error.

retain_on_rollback.description: When `true`, a triggered rollback leaves this publisher's work in place and does not try to undo it. Default `false`.

silent_switch.description:
Silent-install switch string emitted as `InstallerSwitches.Silent` for actual installers (`wix`/`msi`/`exe`/`nsis`). When unset, anodizer derives the switch from the installer type (`/quiet` for msi, `/S` for exe/nsis). Never emitted for `zip`/`portable` artifacts.

Example: `silent_switch: "/qn"`.

skip_upload.description: Skip publishing. `"true"` always skips; `"auto"` skips for prereleases. Accepts bool or template string.

update_existing_pr.description: When true, force-push the updated manifest to the existing PR branch when a PR for the same head branch already exists. The PR content is updated in place, so no duplicate is created. When false (default), the push is skipped and a warning is emitted so the operator sees that the publisher did not update the PR.

upgrade_behavior.description:
Installer `UpgradeBehavior` for every installer entry. winget accepts `install`, `uninstallPrevious`, and `deny`. Defaults to `install` — the correct behavior for portable-zip CLI tools (`uninstallPrevious` forces a clobbering reinstall).

Example: `upgrade_behavior: "uninstallPrevious"`.

url_template.description: Custom URL template for download URLs (overrides release URL).

architectures.description:
Architecture scope: attach this dependency only to installers whose architecture matches one of these WinGet architecture names (`x64`, `arm64`, `x86`). When unset or empty the dependency applies to every installer (the default — preserves the manifest-wide behavior).

Use this when a runtime dependency is architecture-specific: e.g. an `x64` build needs the x64 VC++ runtime while the native `arm64` build needs the arm64 one, so each must be scoped to its own installer and left off the others.

Example:

```yaml
dependencies:
  - package_identifier: "Microsoft.VCRedist.2015+.x64"
    architectures: ["x64"]
  - package_identifier: "Microsoft.VCRedist.2015+.arm64"
    architectures: ["arm64"]
  # unscoped — applies to every installer:
  - package_identifier: "Acme.CommonRuntime"
```

minimum_version.description: Minimum required version of the dependency.

package_identifier.description: WinGet package identifier of the dependency (e.g., "Publisher.App").

WingetDocumentation.description: A single documentation link rendered into the winget locale manifest's `Documentations[]` block as `{ DocumentLabel, DocumentUrl }`.

label.description: Display label for the link (e.g. `FAQ`, `User Guide`).

url.description: Target URL for the documentation entry.

WingetLocaleConfig.description: One additional locale manifest of a WinGet package. Every field but `locale` is optional and falls back to the same-named field of the default locale, so an entry carries only the translated text.

description.description: Full package description for this locale.

homepage.description: Project homepage URL for this locale.

installation_notes.description: Post-install notes shown to the user for this locale.

locale.description: BCP 47 locale tag stamped into `PackageLocale` and the `.locale.<locale>.yaml` file name (e.g. `pt-BR`). Required; supports templates. Must differ from `default_locale` and from every other entry.

package_name.description: Display name shown in the WinGet gallery for this locale.

privacy_url.description: Privacy policy URL for this locale.

publisher_support_url.description: Publisher support URL for this locale.

publisher_url.description: Publisher homepage URL for this locale.

release_notes.description: Release notes for this locale. `Changelog` is available to the template.

release_notes_url.description: URL to the full release notes for this locale.

short_description.description: Short description for this locale (max 256 chars).

tags.description: Tags for this locale (lowercased, spaces replaced with hyphens). An empty or unset list takes the default locale's tags.

WorkspaceConfig.description: A workspace represents an independent project root within a monorepo. Each workspace has its own crates, changelog, and release configuration, allowing independently-versioned components that aren't Cargo workspace members.

after.description: Hooks run after this workspace's pipeline completes.

before.description: Hooks run before this workspace's pipeline starts.

binary_signs.description: Binary-specific signing configs (same shape as `signs` but only for binary artifacts). The `artifacts` field on each entry is constrained at parse time to `binary` / `none` (or omitted) — a broader filter on `binary_signs` would silently match nothing because the loop only iterates Binary artifacts. Constraint lives in `deserialize_binary_signs`.

env.description:
Environment variables scoped to this workspace.

List of `KEY=VALUE` strings. Order is preserved. Values are template-rendered at pipeline startup.

name.description: Workspace identifier used in logs and template variables.

signs.description: Signing configurations for binaries, archives, and checksums.

skip.description: Pipeline stages to skip when releasing this workspace. Stage names match the CLI `--skip` flag (e.g., `announce`, `publish`).
